Eq. 1.1 Aether Field Decomposition (Foundational): Splits the field into an inert ambient value and the ripple that does the work
Ae(x, t) = Ae_0 + dAe(x, t)
where Ae: The aether field; Ae_0: The ambient, uniform, inexhaustible value of the aether field — inert on its own; never drawn down by a casting; dAe: The local perturbation (ripple) superimposed on Ae_0 at the moment and place of a casting — the only part of the field that ever does anything

Eq. 1.2 Ripple Sourcing and Propagation (Foundational): How a caster's source current spreads through the aether layer
dAe(x, t) = Int[ G(x, x'; t, t'; g) * J_cast(x', t') ] d4x'
where dAe: The local perturbation (ripple) superimposed on Ae_0 at the moment and place of a casting — the only part of the field that ever does anything; G: The propagator: how strongly and after what delay a disturbance sourced at one point is felt at another, given the geometry g; g: Spacetime metric; J_cast: The source current the caster's invocation injects into the aether field — phi_actual in its role as a physical source

Eq. 1.3 Surface Coupling (Foundational): The three channels through which a ripple pushes on the upper fields
delta(F_f)  = k_f  * dAe(x, t)                         -- gauge-sector distortion
delta(M_op) = c_M  * dAe(x, t)                         -- quark-sector distortion
delta(g)    = Xi(Ae, g),   with Ae = Ae_0 + dAe        -- metric-sector distortion
where delta(F_f): The three coupling channels: gauge-sector, quark-sector and metric-sector distortions produced by a ripple; F_f: Field-strength tensor for force *f*; k_f: Coupling constant, force *f* ∈ {EM, weak, strong, gravity}; dAe: The local perturbation (ripple) superimposed on Ae_0 at the moment and place of a casting — the only part of the field that ever does anything; M_op: Mass operator (matrix form) acting on the quark field; c_M: Matter-coupling constant analogous to k_f, folded into M_op's own definition rather than tracked separately; g: Spacetime metric; Xi(Ae, g): Aether–spacetime coupling term; Ae: The aether field; Ae_0: The ambient, uniform, inexhaustible value of the aether field — inert on its own; never drawn down by a casting

Eq. 1.4 Propagator Self-Dependence (Foundational): Why the metric channel reshapes the medium its own ripple travels through
G(x, x'; t, t'; g)   depends explicitly on g

delta(g) = Xi(Ae, g)   whenever the metric channel is engaged

=>  G(x, x'; t, t'; g + delta(g))  !=  G(x, x'; t, t'; g)
where G: The propagator: how strongly and after what delay a disturbance sourced at one point is felt at another, given the geometry g; g: Spacetime metric; delta(F_f): The three coupling channels: gauge-sector, quark-sector and metric-sector distortions produced by a ripple; Xi(Ae, g): Aether–spacetime coupling term; Ae: The aether field

Eq. 3.1 Grand Unified Aether Equation (Foundational): Master path-integral governing all aether effects
A_op = Loop_dM[ Dpath(Ae) * exp( (i/hbar) * Action ) ]
where A_op: The reality-selection amplitude the Grand Equation evaluates; Loop_dM[...]: Path-integral selection restricted to the caster's comprehension domain dM; Dpath(Ae): Integration measure over aether field configurations; Ae: The aether field; hbar: Action quantum setting the phase scale of the path integral; Action: The aether action: L_total integrated over all of spacetime

Eq. 3.1a Aether Action (Foundational): The action functional integrated inside the path integral
Action = Int[ sqrt(-g) * L_total ] d4x
where Action: The aether action: L_total integrated over all of spacetime; g: Spacetime metric; L_total: The total Lagrangian density and its gauge and quark pieces

Eq. 3.1b Total Lagrangian Density (Foundational): Sum of the gauge, quark, and aether-geometry contributions
L_total = L_gauge + L_quark + Xi(Ae, g)
where L_total: The total Lagrangian density and its gauge and quark pieces; L_gauge: The total Lagrangian density and its gauge and quark pieces; L_quark: The total Lagrangian density and its gauge and quark pieces; Xi(Ae, g): Aether–spacetime coupling term; Ae: The aether field; g: Spacetime metric

Eq. 3.1c Gauge Term (Foundational): The four fundamental forces' contribution to the density
L_gauge = Sum_f[ k_f * Tr(F_f . F_f) ]
where L_gauge: The total Lagrangian density and its gauge and quark pieces; k_f: Coupling constant, force *f* ∈ {EM, weak, strong, gravity}; F_f: Field-strength tensor for force *f*

Eq. 3.1d Quark Term (Foundational): Matter's contribution to the density
L_quark = q_bar * (i*gam^u*D_u - M_op) * q
where L_quark: The total Lagrangian density and its gauge and quark pieces; q_bar: Quark field and its Dirac conjugate; M_op: Mass operator (matrix form) acting on the quark field; q: Quark field and its Dirac conjugate

Eq. 3.2 Fidelity-Weighted Output (Foundational): Scales any term's effective output by execution precision
X_eff = X_ideal * Fid(t_ins)
Fid   = | <phi_ideal | phi_actual(t_ins)> |^2
0 <= Fid <= 1
where X_eff: Theoretical output of a fully solved term, and the effective output actually produced — X_ideal scaled by Fid; X_ideal: Theoretical output of a fully solved term, and the effective output actually produced — X_ideal scaled by Fid; Fid: Fidelity coefficient — overlap between ideal and actual invocation; t_ins: Time invested in inscribing/invoking a term; phi_ideal: Ideal formal structure of a term vs. the caster's real-time invocation of it; phi_actual: Ideal formal structure of a term vs. the caster's real-time invocation of it

Eq. 3.4 Unassisted Fidelity Ceiling (Foundational): Governs casting a solved term with no physical medium
Fid_max(x, anchor) = Fid_max(x) * ( anchor + (1 - anchor) * Step( prac(x) - prac_min ) )
where anchor: 1 if a physical medium is used, 0 for pure mental visualization; Step(...): Heaviside step function; prac(x): Practice depth for a specific term x; prac_min: Mastery threshold required for unassisted invocation

Eq. 3.5 Simulated Invocation (Foundational): Evaluates an invocation's readout without committing it to reality
Sim[ X ](t_ins) -> { Fid(t_ins), X_eff_proj, E_back_proj }
Loop_dM[ ... ]  not evaluated
where Sim[...]: Prefix operator: evaluates an invocation's readout without committing it to reality; t_ins: Time invested in inscribing/invoking a term; Fid: Fidelity coefficient — overlap between ideal and actual invocation; X_eff_proj: Projected effective output under Sim[...] — identical math to X_eff, never released; E_back_proj: Projected backlash energy under Sim[...] — identical math to E_back, never released; Loop_dM[...]: Path-integral selection restricted to the caster's comprehension domain dM

Eq. 3.1e Partial Diagonalization (Artisan): A finite, proven subset of `M_op`'s eigenvectors
M_op_partial = Sum_{i in S} lam_i * |e_i><e_i|
where M_op_partial: An Artisan's partially diagonalized mass operator, and the finite eigenvector subset it's built from; S: An Artisan's partially diagonalized mass operator, and the finite eigenvector subset it's built from; lam_i: Eigenvalue/eigenvector pair of M_op; lam_i is solved exactly for e_i when e_i in S; e_i: Eigenvalue/eigenvector pair of M_op; lam_i is solved exactly for e_i when e_i in S

Eq. 3.1f Perturbative Aether-Geometry Coupling (Warden): Leading-order expansion of `Xi(Ae, g)` around flat space
Xi_pert(Ae, g) = Xi_0 + eps * Xi_1 + O(eps^2)
where Xi_pert: A Warden's perturbative expansion of Xi(Ae, g), and its departure-from-flat-space parameter; Ae: The aether field; g: Spacetime metric; Xi_0: The leading terms of a Warden's perturbative expansion of Xi(Ae, g) around flat space; eps: A Warden's perturbative expansion of Xi(Ae, g), and its departure-from-flat-space parameter; Xi_1: The leading terms of a Warden's perturbative expansion of Xi(Ae, g) around flat space

Eq. 3.1g Domain Persistence (Sovereign/Legend): Spatial and temporal reach of a solved `Xi(Ae, g)`
Xi_valid(x, t):  |x - x0| < R_dom   and   t < t_dom
where Xi_valid: Where and when a solved Xi(Ae, g) remains valid: inside R_dom, before t_dom; R_dom: Spatial radius and duration over which a solved Xi(Ae, g) remains valid — small for Sovereign, effectively permanent for Legend; t_dom: Spatial radius and duration over which a solved Xi(Ae, g) remains valid — small for Sovereign, effectively permanent for Legend

Eq. 4.0a Thermal Excitation (Novice): Injects power into a substance via EM coupling ("boiling water")
P_in = k_EM * Fid * Ae_local^2
dT/dt = P_in / (m * c_p)
where P_in: Power injected into a target substance; k_EM: The electromagnetic coupling constant — one of the four k_f terms; the first any student solves; Fid: Fidelity coefficient — overlap between ideal and actual invocation; Ae_local: Locally concentrated aether density at a point of contact

Eq. 4.0b Minor Levitation (Novice): Partially cancels local weight via gravitational coupling
F_net = m_obj * g_local * (1 - k_grav * Fid)
where F_net: Net downward force remaining after partial gravitational cancellation; m_obj: Mass of the object being lifted, and the local gravitational acceleration acting on it; g_local: Mass of the object being lifted, and the local gravitational acceleration acting on it; k_grav: The gravitational coupling constant — one of the four k_f terms; a force-coupling, not the metric itself; Fid: Fidelity coefficient — overlap between ideal and actual invocation

Eq. 4.0c Minor Cohesion Boost (Novice): Temporarily boosts a material's binding energy
E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 + k_strong * Fid)
where E_bind_eff: A material's ordinary binding energy, and its temporarily boosted value; E_bind: A material's ordinary binding energy, and its temporarily boosted value; k_strong: The strong-force coupling constant — one of the four k_f terms; Fid: Fidelity coefficient — overlap between ideal and actual invocation

Eq. 4.0e Ripple Sense (Novice): Passive detection use of the `k_EM` channel; a read rather than a source
S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t)          -- read-only; no delta(F_EM) is sourced
where S_detect: Passive detection readout and the nearby ripple it reads, using the k_EM channel in reverse; k_EM: The electromagnetic coupling constant — one of the four k_f terms; the first any student solves; dAe_nearby: Passive detection readout and the nearby ripple it reads, using the k_EM channel in reverse

Eq. 4.13 Sequential Invocation Overhead (Journeyman): Formalizes the disjoint activation windows and switching cost (`tau_switch`) between two un-cross-coupled `k_f` terms
X_seq(t) = X_1(x,t) * Win_1(t) + X_2(x,t) * Win_2(t)
Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0   for all t
tau_switch = t_start(Win_2) - t_end(Win_1)
where X_seq: Total Journeyman output over time — a sum of non-overlapping contributions; X_1: Any two solved Novice-tier expressions held in sequence by a Journeyman; Win_1(t): Activation-window indicator functions (1 while a given solved k_f term is actively producing output, 0 otherwise); mutually exclusive at Journeyman tier since no Chi(f1,f2) exists to let one ripple satisfy both channels of Eq. 1.3 at once; X_2: Any two solved Novice-tier expressions held in sequence by a Journeyman; Win_2(t): Activation-window indicator functions (1 while a given solved k_f term is actively producing output, 0 otherwise); mutually exclusive at Journeyman tier since no Chi(f1,f2) exists to let one ripple satisfy both channels of Eq. 1.3 at once; tau_switch: Dead time between two sequential Journeyman castings, spent re-inscribing or re-visualizing (§3.6); shrinks with drilled practice but cannot structurally reach zero without Chi

Eq. 4.14 Cross-Coupling Function (Adept): Formal overlap measure defining `Chi(f1,f2)`; `Chi = 0` is exactly the Journeyman condition
Chi(f1, f2) = Overlap[ delta(F_f1), delta(F_f2) ; dAe ]      0 <= Chi <= 1
where Chi(f1, f2): Solved cross-coupling function joining two forces; absent at Journeyman tier, present at Adept; delta(F_f): The three coupling channels: gauge-sector, quark-sector and metric-sector distortions produced by a ripple; dAe: The local perturbation (ripple) superimposed on Ae_0 at the moment and place of a casting — the only part of the field that ever does anything

Eq. 4.15 Adept Combined Output (Adept): Promotes the Spell Directory's informal Adept Combination Pattern to the numbered index; `Fid` enters squared because `Chi` measures one ripple against two channels at once
X_combo = k_f1 * k_f2 * Fid^2 * Chi(f1, f2)
where X_combo: An Adept's combined output from one ripple satisfying two gauge channels; Fid: Fidelity coefficient — overlap between ideal and actual invocation; Chi(f1, f2): Solved cross-coupling function joining two forces; absent at Journeyman tier, present at Adept

Eq. 4.16 Eigenvector Draw (Artisan): Quark-sector analogue of Eq. 4.0a; the shared formal backbone behind AR-01–AR-07
Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local,      e_i in S   (S per Eq. 3.1e)
where Effect_i: Magnitude of the quark-sector effect produced by drawing on eigenvector e_i; lam_i: Eigenvalue/eigenvector pair of M_op; lam_i is solved exactly for e_i when e_i in S; Fid: Fidelity coefficient — overlap between ideal and actual invocation; dAe_local: The sourced ripple concentrated at the working site — the same quantity as Ae_local, written in §1.1's perturbation notation; e_i: Eigenvalue/eigenvector pair of M_op; lam_i is solved exactly for e_i when e_i in S; S: An Artisan's partially diagonalized mass operator, and the finite eigenvector subset it's built from

Eq. 4.17 Off-Basis Extrapolation (Artisan): Quark-sector analogue of Eq. 4.7's backlash integral; confirms §1.3's claim that the backlash mechanism is universal
E_back_mat = Int_V[ | lam_guess - lam_true |^2 ] dV,      e_guess not in S
where E_back_mat: Backlash energy absorbed when a caster targets an eigenvector outside S — the quark-sector form of E_back; lam_guess: Assumed vs. actual eigenvalue when a caster targets a material eigenvector outside S; lam_true: Assumed vs. actual eigenvalue when a caster targets a material eigenvector outside S; S: An Artisan's partially diagonalized mass operator, and the finite eigenvector subset it's built from

Eq. 4.18 Full Transmutation (Master): Rewrites a quantity of matter's identity via a unitary operator over the complete `M_op` eigenbasis
M_op_full = Sum_{all i}[ lam_i * |e_i><e_i| ],      S = complete eigenbasis
q_new = U_transmute(M_op_full) * q_old
where lam_i: Eigenvalue/eigenvector pair of M_op; lam_i is solved exactly for e_i when e_i in S; e_i: Eigenvalue/eigenvector pair of M_op; lam_i is solved exactly for e_i when e_i in S; S: An Artisan's partially diagonalized mass operator, and the finite eigenvector subset it's built from; U_transmute(M_op_full): Unitary operator reassigning a quantity of matter's expression across the complete eigenbasis of M_op

Eq. 4.19 Universal Binding & Decay Control (Master): Generalizes Eq. 4.0c/4.0d's single-material boost/nudge to any material, once `c_M` is unrestricted by a partial `S`
E_bind_eff(x) = E_bind(x) * (1 + s * c_M * Fid),        any x  (S complete)
Gamma_eff(x)   = Gamma_0(x) * (1 + s * c_M * Fid)
s = +1 (boost / hasten)  or  s = -1 (weaken / arrest),  chosen at inscription
where E_bind_eff: A material's ordinary binding energy, and its temporarily boosted value; E_bind: A material's ordinary binding energy, and its temporarily boosted value; s: Direction parameter for Universal Binding & Decay Control: +1 to boost/hasten, -1 to weaken/arrest; c_M: Matter-coupling constant analogous to k_f, folded into M_op's own definition rather than tracked separately; Fid: Fidelity coefficient — overlap between ideal and actual invocation; S: An Artisan's partially diagonalized mass operator, and the finite eigenvector subset it's built from; Gamma_eff: Baseline and weak-force-nudged decay rate of trace unstable material; Gamma_0: Baseline and weak-force-nudged decay rate of trace unstable material

Eq. 4.20 Perturbative Curvature Whisper (Warden): Confines a solved `eps*Xi_1` term to a validated neighborhood `R_proven`; the entire practical range of Warden-tier metric effects
delta(g)_warden = eps * Xi_1 * Bump(r, R_proven)
where delta(F_f): The three coupling channels: gauge-sector, quark-sector and metric-sector distortions produced by a ripple; g: Spacetime metric; eps: A Warden's perturbative expansion of Xi(Ae, g), and its departure-from-flat-space parameter; Xi_1: The leading terms of a Warden's perturbative expansion of Xi(Ae, g) around flat space; Bump(r, R): Smooth localization function, ~1 inside radius R, ~0 outside; R_proven: A specific, previously-validated geometry to which a Warden confines an effect via Bump(r, R_proven)

E_back_pert = Int_V[ | Xi(Ae,g) - (Xi_0 + eps*Xi_1) |^2 ] dV,      for  eps > eps_valid(R_proven)

Eq. 4.1 Overlay Identification (Sovereign/Legend): Establishes conformal identification between two coordinates
Xi_overlay(A, B) = Ae*(A) * U_op(A, B) * Ae(B) - Delta( g(A) - Om2(x) * g(B) )
where Ae: The aether field; U_op(A, B): Unitary identification operator between two points; g: Spacetime metric; Om2(x): Conformal scale factor reconciling two locations' metrics

Eq. 4.2 Null-Displacement Constraint (Sovereign/Legend): Guarantees the Overlay Fold is mass-neutral
Loop_traj[ (T_ae - T_mat) ] d(traj) = 0
where T_ae: Stress-energy tensors, aether field vs. physical matter; T_mat: Stress-energy tensors, aether field vs. physical matter

Eq. 4.3 Superposed State Vector (Sovereign/Legend): Describes the caster's state while a fold is held open
|Phi(t)> = a(t)|A> + b(t)|B>
|a|^2 + |b|^2 = 1
a(0) = 1,  b(0) = 0
where a(t): Amplitudes: "still at A" / "arrived at B"; b(t): Amplitudes: "still at A" / "arrived at B"

Eq. 4.4 Fold Evolution (Sovereign/Legend): Governs how holding the fold shifts probability from A to B
i*hbar * d/dt [a; b] = [ [0, U_op(A,B)], [U_op(A,B)*, 0] ] * [a; b]
where hbar: Action quantum setting the phase scale of the path integral; a(t): Amplitudes: "still at A" / "arrived at B"; b(t): Amplitudes: "still at A" / "arrived at B"; U_op(A, B): Unitary identification operator between two points

Eq. 4.5 Resolution Functional (Sovereign/Legend): Probability of clean arrival at release
P_arrive(t_rel) = | <B | Phi(t_rel)> |^2 * exp( -G_dec * t_rel )
where P_arrive: Probability of clean arrival at the moment a fold is released; t_rel: Elapsed hold time at the moment the caster releases the fold — the counterpart to t_ins; G_dec: Decoherence rate governing collapse safety

Eq. 4.6 Decoherence Rate (Sovereign/Legend): Determines collapse safety from knowledge and interference
G_dec = eta * ( mismatch(Om2) )^2 / K(B) + s_int
where G_dec: Decoherence rate governing collapse safety; eta: Proportionality constant setting how strongly conformal mismatch drives decoherence; mismatch(Om2): Mismatch between the caster's assumed and the true conformal factor of the destination; Om2(x): Conformal scale factor reconciling two locations' metrics; K(x): Knowledge coefficient for a given location; s_int: External interference term

Eq. 4.7 Backlash Energy (Sovereign/Legend): Curvature stress absorbed by the caster on failed collapse
E_back = Int_V[ | g(A) - Om2(x) * g(B) |^2 ] dV
where E_back: Curvature-stress energy absorbed on failed collapse; g: Spacetime metric; Om2(x): Conformal scale factor reconciling two locations' metrics

Eq. 4.8 Localized Well Source (Sovereign/Legend): Sources real curvature from aether alone, within a core radius
Curv(g)(r) = Xi(Ae, g) * Bump(r, R_core)
where Curv(g): Curvature built from the metric (Einstein-tensor analogue); g: Spacetime metric; Xi(Ae, g): Aether–spacetime coupling term; Ae: The aether field; Bump(r, R): Smooth localization function, ~1 inside radius R, ~0 outside; R_core: Radius of the well's core (true singularity/horizon region)

Eq. 4.9 Counter-Curvature Shell (Sovereign/Legend): Anti-gravity annulus that cancels the well's exterior field
Curv(g)(r) = -Xi(Ae, g) * Shell(r, R_core, R_shell)      for R_core <= r <= R_shell
where Curv(g): Curvature built from the metric (Einstein-tensor analogue); g: Spacetime metric; Xi(Ae, g): Aether–spacetime coupling term; Ae: The aether field; Shell(r, R1, R2): Smooth annular support function, nonzero only between R1 and R2; R_core: Radius of the well's core (true singularity/horizon region); R_shell: Outer containment radius — the intended edge of the well's influence

Eq. 4.10 Containment Lapse & Horizon Tuning (Sovereign/Legend): Engineers a genuine, causally sealing horizon at the shell boundary
lapse(r) = sqrt( 1 - 2*k_newton*M_ae(r) / r )      for R_core <= r <= R_shell
lapse(R_shell) -> 0   when   2*k_newton*M_ae(R_shell) = R_shell
where lapse(r): Proper-time rate at radius r relative to the exterior; k_newton: Fixed background constant governing how strongly mass-energy curves spacetime (a Newton's-constant analogue) — distinct from the solvable gauge coupling k_grav (Eq. 3.1c); no caster solves or scales it; M_ae(r): Enclosed aether-mass-equivalent within radius r; R_core: Radius of the well's core (true singularity/horizon region); R_shell: Outer containment radius — the intended edge of the well's influence

Eq. 4.11 Residual Outreach (Sovereign/Legend): Leaked field from imperfect shell fidelity, as a higher multipole
Curv_ext(r) = (1 - Fid_shell) * Xi(Ae, g)|_{R_core} / r^3      for r > R_shell
where Curv_ext(r): Residual external curvature from an imperfectly contained well; Fid_shell: Fidelity coefficient specific to the counter-curvature shell (Eq. 4.9); Xi(Ae, g): Aether–spacetime coupling term; Ae: The aether field; g: Spacetime metric; R_core: Radius of the well's core (true singularity/horizon region); R_shell: Outer containment radius — the intended edge of the well's influence

Eq. 4.12 Unified Bound Singularity Form (Sovereign/Legend): Condenses Eq. 4.8, 4.9, and 4.11 into one piecewise definition
Curv(g)(r) = Xi(Ae,g) * [ Bump(r,R_core) - Shell(r,R_core,R_shell) ]
             + (1 - Fid_shell) * Xi(Ae,g)|_{R_core} * r^-3 * Step(r - R_shell)

subject to:  lapse(r) = sqrt(1 - 2*k_newton*M_ae(r)/r)
             lapse(R_shell) -> 0   when   2*k_newton*M_ae(R_shell) = R_shell
where Curv(g): Curvature built from the metric (Einstein-tensor analogue); g: Spacetime metric; Xi(Ae, g): Aether–spacetime coupling term; Ae: The aether field; Bump(r, R): Smooth localization function, ~1 inside radius R, ~0 outside; R_core: Radius of the well's core (true singularity/horizon region); Shell(r, R1, R2): Smooth annular support function, nonzero only between R1 and R2; R_shell: Outer containment radius — the intended edge of the well's influence; Fid_shell: Fidelity coefficient specific to the counter-curvature shell (Eq. 4.9); Step(...): Heaviside step function; lapse(r): Proper-time rate at radius r relative to the exterior; k_newton: Fixed background constant governing how strongly mass-energy curves spacetime (a Newton's-constant analogue) — distinct from the solvable gauge coupling k_grav (Eq. 3.1c); no caster solves or scales it; M_ae(r): Enclosed aether-mass-equivalent within radius r

Eq. 4.22 Standing Fold Persistence (Legend): Reuses Eq. 4.1 unchanged under Eq. 3.1g's scaling; introduces `t_drift` as the operative Legend-tier constraint
Xi_overlay_legend(A,B) = Xi_overlay(A,B)   [Eq. 4.1],   subject to R_dom, t_dom -> t_dom_legend   (Eq. 3.1g)
t_drift = interval between re-validations of Om2(x) at B required to keep mismatch(Om2) below G_dec's safe threshold (Eq. 4.6)
where R_dom: Spatial radius and duration over which a solved Xi(Ae, g) remains valid — small for Sovereign, effectively permanent for Legend; t_dom: Spatial radius and duration over which a solved Xi(Ae, g) remains valid — small for Sovereign, effectively permanent for Legend; t_dom_legend: The t_dom value at Legend scale — a standing duration (years to a generation) rather than a Sovereign's bounded hold; t_drift: Interval between re-validations of a destination's true conformal factor Om2(x) needed to keep mismatch(Om2) below G_dec's safe threshold; Om2(x): Conformal scale factor reconciling two locations' metrics; mismatch(Om2): Mismatch between the caster's assumed and the true conformal factor of the destination

Eq. 4.23 Standing Singularity & Recertification Interval (Legend): Reuses Eq. 4.12 unchanged under Eq. 3.1g's scaling; introduces `t_recert` bounding Eq. 4.11's leak over `t_dom_legend`
Curv(g)_legend(r) = Curv(g)(r)   [Eq. 4.12],   subject to t_dom -> t_dom_legend   (Eq. 3.1g)
t_recert = max interval between Fid_shell re-inscriptions such that Curv_ext(r) (Eq. 4.11) stays below the ambient background noise floor for the singularity's full t_dom_legend
where Curv(g): Curvature built from the metric (Einstein-tensor analogue); g: Spacetime metric; t_dom: Spatial radius and duration over which a solved Xi(Ae, g) remains valid — small for Sovereign, effectively permanent for Legend; t_dom_legend: The t_dom value at Legend scale — a standing duration (years to a generation) rather than a Sovereign's bounded hold; t_recert: Max interval between Fid_shell re-inscriptions such that residual leak Curv_ext(r) stays below the ambient noise floor across t_dom_legend; Fid_shell: Fidelity coefficient specific to the counter-curvature shell (Eq. 4.9); Curv_ext(r): Residual external curvature from an imperfectly contained well

Eq. 4.24 Tetrarch Coherence Fraction (Beyond Legend): Averages all six solved `Chi` pairs as a checkable proxy for closeness to `k_unified`
Coh_tetrarch = average of Chi(f1,f2) over all 6 unordered pairs of {EM, weak, strong, gravity}
Coh_tetrarch -> 1 as k_unified is approached (never reached)
where Coh_tetrarch: Average of the six solved Chi(f1,f2) pairwise values; tends to 1 as k_unified is approached (never reached); Chi(f1, f2): Solved cross-coupling function joining two forces; absent at Journeyman tier, present at Adept; k_unified: Unsolved single coupling that would replace all four k_f terms at once (Tetrarch Path)

Eq. 4.25 Demiurge Bounded Generative Family (Beyond Legend): Counts verified predictions from one proven extrapolation rule, short of full `Gen(dM)`
Gen_partial(dM) = { predicted e_new : e_new derived from S by a proven extrapolation rule r }
N_family = |Gen_partial(dM)|
where Gen_partial(dM): A proven, bounded extrapolation rule predicting new M_op eigenvectors from S, and the count of its verified predictions; dM: Boundary of the caster's comprehension domain; S: An Artisan's partially diagonalized mass operator, and the finite eigenvector subset it's built from; a(t): Amplitudes: "still at A" / "arrived at B"; N_family: A proven, bounded extrapolation rule predicting new M_op eigenvectors from S, and the count of its verified predictions

Eq. 4.26 Cosmographer Domain Ratio (Beyond Legend): Ratio of achieved to Legend-typical domain size; each increment costs more than the last (§1.4)
rho_cosmo = R_dom_achieved / R_dom_legend_typical      (analogously definable for t_dom)
where rho_cosmo: Ratio of a caster's achieved domain to a typical Legend's domain, and the reference domain size it's measured against (Cosmographer Path); R_dom_legend_typical: Ratio of a caster's achieved domain to a typical Legend's domain, and the reference domain size it's measured against (Cosmographer Path); t_dom: Spatial radius and duration over which a solved Xi(Ae, g) remains valid — small for Sovereign, effectively permanent for Legend

Eq. 4.27 Communion Pooled Boundary Ratio (Beyond Legend): Ratio of a Communion's pooled `dM_total` to a typical Legend's `dM`
N_comm = | dM_total | / | dM_legend_typical |
where N_comm: Ratio of a Communion's pooled dM_total to a typical Legend's dM, and that reference quantity; dM_total: Union of several casters' individually-proven comprehension domains (Communion Path); dM_legend_typical: Ratio of a Communion's pooled dM_total to a typical Legend's dM, and that reference quantity

[N-EM-01] Spark Draw (Novice, EM). V_out = k_EM * Fid * Ae_local A small, controlled static discharge (V_out, the discharge potential produced) between the caster's fingers and a target — enough to light kindling, startle, or send a visible signal at range. The first technique most students cast that isn't Eq. 4.0a itself. Working form (Eq. 8.1): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM01 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Spark Draw (N-EM-01): eta_NEM01 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-02] Cold Ember (Novice, EM). P_in = -k_EM * Fid * Ae_local^2 Eq. 4.0a run in reverse: heat is drawn out rather than pushed in. Used for chilling drinks, slowing spoilage over a single evening, or cooling a wagon axle that's started to seize — nothing that would count as preservation at any real timescale. Working form (Eq. 8.2): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM02 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Cold Ember (N-EM-02): eta_NEM02 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-03] Lumen Thread (Novice, EM). L_out = k_EM * Fid * Ae_local(t)   -- held steady rather than discharged A sustained, low, flameless glow (L_out, the luminous output) along a treated wick or thread rather than a single discharge. The caster's main skill here is holding Ae_local constant over time instead of releasing it all at once — an early, gentle introduction to sustained casting. Working form (Eq. 8.3): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM03 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Lumen Thread (N-EM-03): eta_NEM03 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-04] Static Ward (Novice, EM). A faint, continuous repulsive charge held at the skin or on clothing — deflects dust, light debris, and insects. Popular with travelers, archivists, and anyone else who spends their day around things they'd rather not carry home. Working form (Eq. 8.4): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM04 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Static Ward (N-EM-04): eta_NEM04 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-05] Ripple Sense (Novice, EM). S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) Eq. 4.0e. A passive, continuous read on the same k_EM channel every other EM technique here actively sources into — the caster notices a nearby working before an ordinary bystander would feel its heat, light, or static. Costs nothing and carries no fizzle or backlash risk (Eq. 4.0e), since nothing is ever sourced; the limitation is purely informational, not mechanical. Gravity (k_grav) — extends Eq. 4.0b. Working form (Eq. 8.5): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM05 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Ripple Sense (N-EM-05): eta_NEM05 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-GR-01] Feather Fall (Novice, Gravity). F_net = m_obj * g_local * (1 - k_grav * Fid),  Fid < 1 by design The same equation as Eq. 4.0b, deliberately undershot — a controlled slow descent rather than full cancellation. Taught before full levitation precisely because undershooting on purpose is safer to practice than aiming for zero and occasionally overshooting into a shove. Working form (Eq. 8.6): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR01) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Feather Fall (N-GR-01): eta_NGR01 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-02] Anchor Step (Novice, Gravity). F_net = m_obj * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid) The inverse of Eq. 4.0b: a temporary increase in effective weight at the caster's own feet, for better footing on ice, a listing deck, or a narrow ledge in wind. Working form (Eq. 8.7): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR02) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Anchor Step (N-GR-02): eta_NGR02 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-03] Light Load (Novice, Gravity). Eq. 4.0b applied to a carried object rather than the caster — a porter's or packer's trick, and one of the first Novice techniques to see routine commercial use rather than staying purely in a training hall. Strong (k_strong) — extends Eq. 4.0c. Working form (Eq. 8.8): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 - k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR03) v_term = sqrt(2 * F_net * h_drop / m_t) Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Light Load (N-GR-03): eta_NGR03 is the share of the fall the caster catches, set by how soon the ripple reaches the thing.

[N-ST-01] Seal Bind (Novice, Strong). E_bind_eff(x) = E_bind(x) * (1 + k_strong * Fid),  applied only at contact point x Eq. 4.0c narrowed to a single point of contact between two surfaces — rope ends, a cracked seam, torn fibers held together — rather than a whole object's bulk cohesion. Fails safely: a dropped Fid just loosens the join rather than fusing it wrong. Working form (Eq. 8.9): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST01) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Seal Bind (N-ST-01): eta_NST01 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-ST-02] Brittle Ease (Novice, Strong). E_bind_eff(x) = E_bind(x) * (1 - k_strong * Fid) The deliberate inverse of Eq. 4.0c — a small, precise weakening at one point, for a clean split rather than a ragged one. Common among fletchers, coopers, and quarry hands. Weak (k_weak) — extends Eq. 4.0d. Working form (Eq. 8.10): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST02) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Brittle Ease (N-ST-02): eta_NST02 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-WK-01] Quick Ripen (Novice, Weak). Eq. 4.0d's decay nudge applied to already-ripening produce, nudging a process already underway forward by a day or two rather than starting one from nothing. An orchard-keeper's convenience, not a transformation. Working form (Eq. 8.11): Gamma_eff = Gamma_0 * (1 + k_weak * Fid * eta_NWK01) t_cure = t_cure_0 * Gamma_0 / Gamma_eff Working form of Eq. 4.0d for Quick Ripen (N-WK-01): eta_NWK01 is how much of the cure's slow chemistry answers to the nudge; some processes barely do, and the entry says so.

[N-WK-02] Faint Ward-Light (Novice, Weak). Eq. 4.0d held at the lowest sustainable output — a dim, steady, personal glow rather than a burst of warmth. The standard "still breathing" marker-light for anyone working somewhere that a torch would be a liability: mines, powder stores, night watches. Working form (Eq. 8.12): Gamma_eff = Gamma_0 * (1 + k_weak * Fid * eta_NWK02) P_out = Gamma_eff * E_per_decay * N_unstable -- as warmth; held at duty D_cycle Working form of Eq. 4.0d for Faint Ward-Light (N-WK-02): eta_NWK02 is how much of the faint radiant output is kept as warmth rather than lost as glow.

[J-01] Ember Handoff (Journeyman). Eq. 4.0a, then N-GR-03. Heat a coal, then briefly lighten it to toss it accurately. Two separate, complete castings back to back, not one continuous effect. Working form (Eq. 8.13): X_seq(t) = X_Eq4.0a(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NGR03(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Ember Handoff (J-01): the two windows carry Eq. 4.0a and N-GR-03; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-02] Ward and Weld (Journeyman). N-ST-01, then N-ST-02, on different materials in the same working session. A cooper's or fletcher's routine: bind one seam, split one length, never both at once. Working form (Eq. 8.14): X_seq(t) = X_NST01(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NST02(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Ward and Weld (J-02): the two windows carry N-ST-01 and N-ST-02; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-03] Lantern-Keeper's Round (Journeyman). N-EM-03 or N-WK-02, chosen by available margin rather than blended between. A night-watch specialty precisely because the choice, not a combination, is the skill being exercised. Working form (Eq. 8.15): X_seq(t) = X_NEM03(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NWK02(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Lantern-Keeper's Round (J-03): the two windows carry N-EM-03 and N-WK-02; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-04] Porter's Relief (Journeyman). N-GR-03 on a companion's litter, N-EM-02 on a wagon axle that's started to seize, applied in turn over the course of a journey rather than together. Working form (Eq. 8.16): X_seq(t) = X_NGR03(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NEM02(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Porter's Relief (J-04): the two windows carry N-GR-03 and N-EM-02; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-05] Two-Handed Smith (Journeyman). Eq. 4.0a to heat the workpiece, then Eq. 4.0c to set the join, in strict alternation for as long as the work lasts. A guild-standard pairing precisely because an Adept's Flash-Forge (below) replaces it with one technique instead of two. Working form (Eq. 8.17): X_seq(t) = X_Eq4.0a(t) * Win_1(t) + X_Eq4.0c(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Two-Handed Smith (J-05): the two windows carry Eq. 4.0a and Eq. 4.0c; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-06] Watch-Fire Relay (Journeyman). Eq. 4.0a to relight a signal fire, N-EM-01 for a brief, bright flash where a full fire would be too slow. A chain of watchers relaying a message this way is switching, station to station, never combining. Working form (Eq. 8.18): X_seq(t) = X_Eq4.0a(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NEM01(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Watch-Fire Relay (J-06): the two windows carry Eq. 4.0a and N-EM-01; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-07] Bladeline Feint (Journeyman). N-GR-01, then N-EM-01, drilled by duelists to the smallest tau_switch (Eq. 4.13) a Journeyman can sustain: lighten the step mid-lunge, then snap a startling spark at the guard the instant the lightening window closes. The tightness of the gap is the entire training regimen — and precisely how close it can get to zero without ever reaching it is the standing proof the duelist is still Journeyman, not Adept. Working form (Eq. 8.19): X_seq(t) = X_NGR01(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NEM01(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Bladeline Feint (J-07): the two windows carry N-GR-01 and N-EM-01; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[AD-01] Flash-Forge (Adept, EM+Strong). Heating and cohesion-boosting blended into one continuous pass rather than Two-Handed Smith's two separate steps (J-05). The signature technique of any smith who's made Adept, and usually the reason they're described that way rather than as "a very fast Journeyman." Working form (Eq. 8.20): X_combo = k_EM * k_strong * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Strong) * eta_AD01 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Flash-Forge (AD-01), on the EM + Strong pair: eta_AD01 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-02] Storm-Step (Adept, EM+Gravity). A static discharge and a lightened stance blended into a single short, controlled leap kicked off by the discharge itself. Popular with couriers and scouts for the same reason Ember Handoff (J-01) isn't: no visible gap between the spark and the motion. Working form (Eq. 8.21): X_combo = k_EM * k_gravity * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Gravity) * eta_AD02 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Storm-Step (AD-02), on the EM + Gravity pair: eta_AD02 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-03] Cinder-Fall (Adept, EM+Weak). Heat injection blended with a decay nudge to produce a sustained, low, self-feeding flame from poor fuel — damp wood, old peat. Unglamorous and widely taught to Adept-tier quartermasters precisely because it's useful rather than impressive. Working form (Eq. 8.22): X_combo = k_EM * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Weak) * eta_AD03 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Cinder-Fall (AD-03), on the EM + Weak pair: eta_AD03 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-04] Sunder Weight (Adept, Gravity+Strong). The inverse of Light Load blended with Brittle Ease: an object made heavier and more fragile in the same casting. A demolition specialist's standard tool. Working form (Eq. 8.23): X_combo = k_gravity * k_strong * Fid^2 * Chi(Gravity, Strong) * eta_AD04 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Sunder Weight (AD-04), on the Gravity + Strong pair: eta_AD04 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-05] Quiet Mend (Adept, Strong+Weak). A cohesion boost blended with Eq. 4.0d run in reverse, slowing rather than hastening decay, to stabilize an already-aging bind — old rope, brittle leather — rather than merely strengthening a fresh one. A preservationist's or archivist's technique, and one of the few Adept combinations built around slowing something down. Working form (Eq. 8.24): X_combo = k_strong * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(Strong, Weak) * eta_AD05 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Quiet Mend (AD-05), on the Strong + Weak pair: eta_AD05 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-06] Grave Lantern (Adept, Gravity+Weak). Light Load blended with Faint Ward-Light so a marked object hovers just barely off true rest while glowing faintly. Ceremonial rather than practical; several regional death-rites use a version of this over a grave-marker or a burial buoy. All six unordered force-pairs are exhausted by AD-01 through AD-06 above — there is no seventh pair among four forces. An Adept's remaining growth from here is depth (Fid, practice) on the pairs they hold, solving any of the six they do not yet hold (§4.6 — tier is a per-pair predicate), or reaching for a different channel entirely (Artisan's delta(M_op)); what it is never is a brand-new combination beyond the six. Working form (Eq. 8.25): X_combo = k_gravity * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(Gravity, Weak) * eta_AD06 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Grave Lantern (AD-06), on the Gravity + Weak pair: eta_AD06 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AR-01] Artisan of Salt (Artisan, Salt). The solved eigenvector governs salt's crystal lattice: precise purification, preservation, or selective dissolution and reformation of salt-based compounds. Does not extend to sugar or quartz, whatever their surface similarity. Working form (Eq. 8.26): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR01, e_i in S_AR01 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Salt (AR-01): S_AR01 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR01 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-02] Artisan of Iron (Artisan, Iron). A solved eigenvector for iron's lattice lets a warped blade be trued or its temper shifted without a forge. Bronze and silver are unmodeled and are not touched. Working form (Eq. 8.27): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR02, e_i in S_AR02 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Iron (AR-02): S_AR02 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR02 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-03] Artisan of Bone (Artisan, Bone). A solved eigenvector for bone's mineral structure, used by menders and, less happily, morticians, to realign or preserve it precisely. One of the more common Artisan specialties in settlements without ready access to a trained surgeon — and, per §3.3, exactly as narrow as every other entry here. Working form (Eq. 8.28): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR03, e_i in S_AR03 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Bone (AR-03): S_AR03 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR03 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-04] Artisan of Rot (Artisan, Rot). Not a strengthening eigenvector but a specific, solved decay pathway in organic matter: controlled composting, curing, tanning. A closely guarded trade secret among tanners and vintners rather than a battlefield technique. Working form (Eq. 8.29): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR04, e_i in S_AR04 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Rot (AR-04): S_AR04 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR04 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-05] Artisan of Glass (Artisan, Glass). A solved eigenvector for silica's amorphous structure allows cold reshaping without a furnace. Prized by lens-makers and glaziers, and nearly useless for anything crystalline, since glass's structure is specifically the thing that's been solved. Working form (Eq. 8.30): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR05, e_i in S_AR05 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Glass (AR-05): S_AR05 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR05 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-06] Artisan of Ash (Artisan, Ash). Rare, and largely ceremonial: a solved eigenvector for post-combustion residue lets a caster bind ash into a temporary, brittle shape. Associated almost exclusively with funerary sculpture in the few traditions that still practice it. Working form (Eq. 8.31): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR06, e_i in S_AR06 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Ash (AR-06): S_AR06 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR06 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-07] Artisan of Clay (Artisan, Clay). A solved eigenvector for clay's mineral lattice lets a caster drive precise, localized vitrification — true firing without a kiln — via Eq. 4.16, shaping and hardening a vessel wall by wall rather than all at once in a single heat-soak. Porcelain and stoneware bodies are close cousins but unmodeled, and firing them on the strength of clay's lam_i risks Eq. 4.17's off-basis backlash rather than a merely uneven glaze. Working form (Eq. 8.32): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR07, e_i in S_AR07 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Clay (AR-07): S_AR07 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR07 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[M-01] Full Mend (Master). Eq. 4.19's binding-energy term applied broadly across living tissue rather than to one bound seam: E_bind_eff(x) raised (Eq. 4.19 with s = +1) over an entire injury site at once. Where an Artisan of Bone can only realign what their one solved eigenvector covers, a Master's complete S lets the same boost reach muscle, vessel, and bone together in a single casting. Working form (Eq. 8.33): E_bind_eff(x) = E_bind(x) * (1 + s * c_M * Fid * eta_M01) Gamma_eff(x) = Gamma_0(x) * (1 + s * c_M * Fid * eta_M01), s = -1 (S complete) Working form of Eq. 4.19 for Full Mend (M-01): eta_M01 is the share of the domain the standing presence covers.

[M-02] Grave Turn (Master). Eq. 4.19 turned toward reinforcement (s = -1 on Gamma_eff to arrest decay) or hastened aging (s = +1) of ordinary matter, rather than the dramatic identity swaps of Eq. 4.18 that Masters are best known for. A quarry-hand's or embalmer's use of the same complete eigenbasis that, wielded through U_transmute instead, changes lead to gold — proof the tier's machinery is general-purpose, not spectacle-only. Working form (Eq. 8.34): E_bind_eff(x) = E_bind(x) * (1 + s * c_M * Fid * eta_M02) Gamma_eff(x) = Gamma_0(x) * (1 + s * c_M * Fid * eta_M02), s = -1 (S complete) Working form of Eq. 4.19 for Grave Turn (M-02): eta_M02 is the share of the domain the standing presence covers.

[W-01] Threshold Ease (Warden). Applies Eq. 4.20 to a single, specific, previously-mapped threshold (a doorway or gate), briefly reducing the effective weight of crossing it; R_proven is that one threshold and no other, and the effect ends abruptly at its bounds. Pushing eps past eps_valid(R_proven) risks Eq. 4.21's backlash rather than a merely weaker effect. Working form (Eq. 8.35): delta(g)_W01 = eps * Xi_1 * Bump(r, R_proven) * G_site eps <= eps_valid(R_proven) (Eq. 4.21) Working form of Eq. 4.20 for Threshold Ease (W-01): G_site is the proven geometry's site factor, fixed by its survey.

[LG-01] The Standing Fold (Legend). An inhabited, permanent Overlay linking two settlements, built on the unmodified Eq. 4.1 identification and held open across t_dom_legend. A hereditary order resurveys B's true conformal factor on a t_drift cadence (Eq. 4.22) so mismatch(Om2) never creeps G_dec toward collapse; the order's real craft is scheduling, not spellwork. Working form (Eq. 8.36): Xi_overlay_LG01(A, B) = Xi_overlay(A, B) [Eq. 4.1], t_dom -> t_dom_legend t_drift = L_dom / v_survey * eta_LG01 Working form of Eq. 4.22 for The Standing Fold (LG-01): eta_LG01 is the standing work's upkeep factor.

[LG-02] The Held Star (Legend). A Bound Singularity (Eq. 4.12) maintained for generations as a regional landmark and power source rather than released. Its shell is periodically re-inscribed on a t_recert interval (Eq. 4.23) so the residual field Curv_ext(r) never rises above background and betrays an uncontained mass at range. Working form (Eq. 8.37): Xi_overlay_LG02(A, B) = Xi_overlay(A, B) [Eq. 4.1], t_dom -> t_dom_legend t_drift = L_dom / v_survey * eta_LG02 Working form of Eq. 4.22 for The Held Star (LG-02): eta_LG02 is the standing work's upkeep factor.

[AS-01] The Four-Fold Feint (Beyond Legend). A historical Tetrarch aspirant's signature working, chaining all six solved Chi(f1,f2) pairs in tight, unbroken sequence so that EM, weak, strong, and gravitational expression seemed to flow as one force rather than four. Records treat it as proof Coh_tetrarch (Eq. 4.24) sat near 1 in the caster's hands — and, in the same breath, as proof that k_unified was never actually reached, since the technique still required four couplings performed seamlessly rather than one coupling performed at all. Working form (Eq. 8.38): Coh_tetrarch_AS01 = average of Chi(f1, f2) over the pairs the aspirant held, -> 1 never reached Working form of Eq. 4.24 for The Four-Fold Feint (AS-01): the fragment's measured closeness proxy.

[AS-02] The Bound Chorus (Beyond Legend). A historical Communion working in which several practitioners pooled their individually-proven dM_total into a single acting boundary for one collective casting, reaching an effect no single member's comprehension could have supported alone. Surviving accounts treat it as both the clearest proof N_comm (Eq. 4.27) can exceed 1 and a cautionary tale, since what was merged was the provers themselves, not merely their proofs. --- Working form (Eq. 8.39): rho_cosmo_AS02 = R_dom_achieved / R_dom_legend_typical Working form of Eq. 4.26 for The Bound Chorus (AS-02): the fragment's measured closeness proxy.

[N-EM-06] Kettle's Patience (Novice, EM). P_in = k_EM * Fid * Ae_local^2,   Ae_local held deliberately low over t_hold Eq. 4.0a throttled rather than released — a low, even simmer held for as long as the caster maintains the inscription. The cook's counterpart to Lumen Thread (N-EM-03): the skill being trained is a steady Ae_local, not a strong one. Working form (Eq. 8.40): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM06 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Kettle's Patience (N-EM-06): eta_NEM06 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-07] Mirror Flash (Novice, EM). A single bright, directional pulse of light — Eq. 4.0a's channel expressed as luminance rather than heat, discharged all at once toward a distant watcher. The standard daytime counterpart to a signal fire, and drilled alongside N-EM-01 in most watch traditions. Working form (Eq. 8.41): P_in = -k_EM * Fid * Ae_local^2 * eta_NEM07 -- reverse-sign casting T(t_hold) = T_0 - |P_in| * t_hold * D_cycle / (m_t * c_p) Working form of Eq. 4.0a for Mirror Flash (N-EM-07): eta_NEM07 is the fraction of the drawn heat the target can give up without frosting, which is what keeps the casting honest.

[N-EM-08] Lodestone Touch (Novice, EM). A weak, temporary magnetization impressed on a small iron object — a needle, a nail, a clasp. The effect fades in hours, which is precisely why compass-makers pay for the permanent article and travelers make do with this one. Working form (Eq. 8.42): P_in = -k_EM * Fid * Ae_local^2 * eta_NEM08 -- reverse-sign casting T(t_hold) = T_0 - |P_in| * t_hold * D_cycle / (m_t * c_p) Working form of Eq. 4.0a for Lodestone Touch (N-EM-08): eta_NEM08 is the fraction of the drawn heat the target can give up without frosting, which is what keeps the casting honest.

[N-EM-09] Chill Locker (Novice, EM). Cold Ember (N-EM-02) held over the interior of a chest or crock for t_hold instead of discharged once. Still nothing that counts as preservation at any real timescale — the difference between this and a Master's decay arrest (Eq. 4.19, s = -1) is the difference between a cool pantry and a stopped clock. Working form (Eq. 8.43): P_in = -k_EM * Fid * Ae_local^2 * eta_NEM09 -- reverse-sign casting T(t_hold) = T_0 - |P_in| * t_hold * D_cycle / (m_t * c_p) Working form of Eq. 4.0a for Chill Locker (N-EM-09): eta_NEM09 is the fraction of the drawn heat the target can give up without frosting, which is what keeps the casting honest.

[N-EM-10] Glow Mark (Novice, EM). A faint luminous trace left on stone or bark, fading over a night. Trail-markers, mine surveyors, and children playing at being mine surveyors. The mark is a slowly-relaxing field distortion, not a substance — it cannot be scraped off, only outwaited. Working form (Eq. 8.44): V_out = k_EM * Fid * Ae_local * eta_NEM10 R_reach = V_out / V_break Working form of Eq. 4.0a for Glow Mark (N-EM-10): eta_NEM10 is how much of the discharge reaches the target rather than leaking to the caster's own sleeve, which is to say the aim.

[N-EM-11] Static Comb (Novice, EM). A reverse-sign casting of N-EM-04's held charge: rather than repelling debris from the caster, it strips accumulated static and clinging dust from cloth, parchment, or fleece drawn past the hand. Archivists' guilds teach it in the first month. Working form (Eq. 8.45): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM11 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Static Comb (N-EM-11): eta_NEM11 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-12] Spark Fence (Novice, EM). A treated cord holding a mild N-EM-01 discharge at any point along its length, released on contact. Startles animals and drowsing apprentices equally; hurts neither. The whole cord is one casting — touching it anywhere closes the same inscription. Working form (Eq. 8.46): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM12 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Spark Fence (N-EM-12): eta_NEM12 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-13] Ember Coax (Novice, EM). Eq. 4.0a at its gentlest, aimed into a nearly-dead fire's remaining coals. Distinguished from simply casting heat at fresh fuel by economy: coaxing a live ember to spread costs a far lower Ae_local than igniting cold wood, which is the entire lesson the technique exists to teach. Working form (Eq. 8.47): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM13 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Ember Coax (N-EM-13): eta_NEM13 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-14] Fever Gauge (Novice, EM). A minimal calibrated pulse of Eq. 4.0a into a body or substance, with the caster reading how quickly the injected warmth disperses. Faster dispersal means wetter, denser, or feverish; slower means dry or cold. A physician's and brewer's rule-of-thumb instrument, honest to about the precision of a practiced hand. Working form (Eq. 8.48): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM14 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Fever Gauge (N-EM-14): eta_NEM14 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-15] Lantern Snuff (Novice, EM). Cold Ember narrowed to a wick — heat pulled from the combustion point until flame can no longer sustain. Cleaner than pinching, safer than blowing, and silent, which is why night-watch curricula pair it with N-EM-03 as a set. Working form (Eq. 8.49): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM15 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Lantern Snuff (N-EM-15): eta_NEM15 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-16] Dew Draw (Novice, EM). A surface chilled below the morning's dew point (N-EM-02 held at low output), collecting drinkable condensate over hours. Yields a cup, not a cistern — but a cup, in the wrong country, has bought this technique its place in every caravan-master's contract. Working form (Eq. 8.50): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM16 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Dew Draw (N-EM-16): eta_NEM16 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-17] Dazzle Ward (Novice, EM). Mirror Flash (N-EM-07) turned defensive: a hard, close flash at an aggressor's eyes. Duelists disdain it, because Ripple Sense (N-EM-05) makes it nearly useless against anyone trained — the working announces itself on the k_EM channel a beat before the light arrives. Working form (Eq. 8.51): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM17 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Dazzle Ward (N-EM-17): eta_NEM17 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-18] Copper Song (Novice, EM). A small current induced in a closed loop of wire, enough to twitch a needle or sound a tiny bell at the far end of the loop. Estates wealthy enough to run wire between wings use it as a summons; the technique itself is a Novice staple, the wire is the luxury. Working form (Eq. 8.52): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM18 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Copper Song (N-EM-18): eta_NEM18 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-19] Frost Etch (Novice, EM). N-EM-02 focused to a fingertip's breadth, walking a line of frost across glass or polished metal. The frost pattern lasts minutes and marks nothing permanently — glaziers use it to sketch a cut before committing, which is also exactly how casting instructors use it to sketch glyphs. Working form (Eq. 8.53): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM19 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Frost Etch (N-EM-19): eta_NEM19 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-20] Hearth Halo (Novice, EM). Eq. 4.0a spread thin across a small room's air rather than concentrated at a point — a few degrees of ambient warmth held for t_hold. Inefficient by design; the same Ae_local at a kettle would boil it. Taught anyway, because holding a diffuse distortion steady is a different skill than holding a concentrated one, and Adept blends will eventually demand both. Working form (Eq. 8.54): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM20 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Hearth Halo (N-EM-20): eta_NEM20 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-21] Signal Thread (Novice, EM). Lumen Thread (N-EM-03) pulsed rather than held steady — a coded flicker readable at line-of-sight range. Every trade consortium and border garrison maintains its own codebook; the technique is common, the codebooks are what get stolen. Working form (Eq. 8.55): S_detect(x, t) = k_EM * dAe_nearby(x, t) * eta_NEM21 -- read-only; nothing is sourced Working form of Eq. 4.0e for Signal Thread (N-EM-21): eta_NEM21 is the caster's trained sensitivity in one setting; a passive read costs nothing and this is the only number in it that can be improved.

[N-EM-22] Sun's Patience (Novice, EM). Kettle's Patience (N-EM-06) applied across racks of sliced fruit, fish, or herb over a full day — drying heat, held low and even. One of the highest-t_hold Novice castings in common use, and a standard endurance exercise for exactly that reason. Working form (Eq. 8.56): V_out = k_EM * Fid * Ae_local * eta_NEM22 R_reach = V_out / V_break Working form of Eq. 4.0a for Sun's Patience (N-EM-22): eta_NEM22 is how much of the discharge reaches the target rather than leaking to the caster's own sleeve, which is to say the aim.

[N-EM-23] Arc Splice (Novice, EM). Spark Draw (N-EM-01) narrowed to a wire junction, fusing a hair-fine join. The Novice edge of what Flash-Forge (AD-01) does wholesale: no cohesion boost accompanies the heat, so the join holds by melt alone and a jeweler's version of this remains honest work rather than a blend. Working form (Eq. 8.57): V_out = k_EM * Fid * Ae_local * eta_NEM23 R_reach = V_out / V_break Working form of Eq. 4.0a for Arc Splice (N-EM-23): eta_NEM23 is how much of the discharge reaches the target rather than leaking to the caster's own sleeve, which is to say the aim.

[N-EM-24] Gleam Lure (Novice, EM). A hovering point of soft light held just above water or among stubble — fish rise to it, moths mob it, and both end up in somebody's basket. Fisherfolk's guilds in three river systems independently claim to have invented it, which probably means nobody did. Working form (Eq. 8.58): L_out = k_EM * Fid * Ae_local(t) * eta_NEM24 -- held, not discharged Working form of Eq. 4.0a for Gleam Lure (N-EM-24): eta_NEM24 is how much of the distortion comes out as visible light rather than warmth, which the caster sets by how narrowly the glow is shaped.

[N-EM-25] Quiet Coil (Novice, EM). A reverse-sign damping held around a delicate instrument — lodestones, fine balances, another caster's inscription-in-progress — suppressing ambient static and stray field noise. The rare Novice technique whose customers are mostly other casters. Gravity (k_grav) — extends Eq. 4.0b. Working form (Eq. 8.59): L_out = k_EM * Fid * Ae_local(t) * eta_NEM25 -- held, not discharged Working form of Eq. 4.0a for Quiet Coil (N-EM-25): eta_NEM25 is how much of the distortion comes out as visible light rather than warmth, which the caster sets by how narrowly the glow is shaped.

[N-GR-04] Steady Hand (Novice, Gravity). Light Load (N-GR-03) at the scale of a single held tool — a scalpel, a brush, an engraver's burin made a fraction of its weight so a tremor moves less mass. Surgeons and forgers of documents prize it equally, a pairing moralists have gotten essays out of for generations. Working form (Eq. 8.60): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR04) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Steady Hand (N-GR-04): eta_NGR04 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-05] Level Set (Novice, Gravity). Anchor Step's increase (N-GR-02) applied to a plumb bob or spirit level, settling its swing in a breath instead of a minute. A surveyor's convenience — and, drilled for speed, a common first exercise in casting on a moving target. Working form (Eq. 8.61): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR05) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Level Set (N-GR-05): eta_NGR05 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-06] Soft Landing (Novice, Gravity). Feather Fall (N-GR-01) cast on falling cargo rather than a falling person. Harder than it sounds: the caster is not riding the object, so range and timing must both be judged from outside. Dockworkers' guilds test it with crockery, publicly. Working form (Eq. 8.62): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR06) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Soft Landing (N-GR-06): eta_NGR06 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-07] Counter Sway (Novice, Gravity). Anchor Step held on a vessel's keel-line in a swell, damping roll. The weight increase is modest; what steadies the boat is that it is constant while the water is not. Ferry crews rate a caster by how long they can hold it, not how hard. Working form (Eq. 8.63): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR07) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Counter Sway (N-GR-07): eta_NGR07 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-08] Ridge Step (Novice, Gravity). Light Load on the caster's own body, held across a climb rather than discharged per-stride. The deliberate complement to Feather Fall: one manages a fall, the other prevents it. Mountain couriers run both as a single drilled sequence — which makes those couriers, formally, Journeymen the day the sequence becomes their habit. Working form (Eq. 8.64): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR08) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Ridge Step (N-GR-08): eta_NGR08 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-09] Cart's Mercy (Novice, Gravity). Light Load on a mired wheel at the moment the team heaves. Timing is the entire technique — a lightened wheel and an unready team accomplishes nothing, which makes this the canonical example in casting schools of a flawless Fid wasted by bad coordination. Working form (Eq. 8.65): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR09) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Cart's Mercy (N-GR-09): eta_NGR09 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-10] Well Draw (Novice, Gravity). Light Load held on a filled bucket for the length of its rise. Utterly unremarkable, universally taught, and by head-count likely the most-cast gravity technique in the world — a standing reminder that the median use of aether is chores. Working form (Eq. 8.66): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR10) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Well Draw (N-GR-10): eta_NGR10 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-11] Ballast Word (Novice, Gravity). Anchor Step on one gunwale, cast and released on a coxswain's call, trimming a hull through a turn. Racing crews treat the caster as a crew position with its own seat and its own verb: to ballast. Working form (Eq. 8.67): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR11) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Ballast Word (N-GR-11): eta_NGR11 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-12] Firm Table (Novice, Gravity). Anchor Step's increase applied to a workpiece instead of the caster — the object clamps itself to the bench under its own borrowed weight. Woodworkers use it where a vise would mar the piece; casting instructors use it because a still target is the kindest possible fidelity drill. Working form (Eq. 8.68): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR12) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Firm Table (N-GR-12): eta_NGR12 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-13] Gentle Toss (Novice, Gravity). Light Load on a thrown line, bag, or grapnel for the first half of its arc, released midflight so it lands true. The release timing is the training value: letting go of a casting cleanly, mid-effect, is a skill Novices otherwise reach Journeyman without acquiring. Working form (Eq. 8.69): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR13) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Gentle Toss (N-GR-13): eta_NGR13 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-14] Restful Weight (Novice, Gravity). Anchor Step at its mildest, spread across a blanket — the pressure of a heavy quilt from an ordinary one. Sanatoriums and nurseries keep a caster on retainer for it. Among the least dramatic entries in this directory, and among the most requested. Working form (Eq. 8.70): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR14) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Restful Weight (N-GR-14): eta_NGR14 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-15] Snow Shed (Novice, Gravity). Light Load across a roof's snow burden while crews work beneath, cast from the ground in sections. The load is lightened, never lifted — a distinction every winter-country guild drills, because an overshot casting that lifts the pack sends it down all at once when the hold ends. Working form (Eq. 8.71): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR15) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Snow Shed (N-GR-15): eta_NGR15 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-16] Ford Keeper (Novice, Gravity). Anchor Step held on the caster's own steps across a current. The river pushes; the crosser simply weighs more than the push. Larger parties cross roped to the one caster holding it, which is why river-guides in fording country are casters by default. Working form (Eq. 8.72): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 + k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR16) -- reverse-sign casting Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Ford Keeper (N-GR-16): eta_NGR16 is how much of the added weight lands on the target's footing rather than its middle, which is what makes it hold.

[N-GR-17] Hawk's Lend (Novice, Gravity). Light Load on a messenger bird for its first climbing seconds off the glove. The bird gains launch height; the effect must end before the bird leaves range. Falconers argue endlessly about whether it helps enough to justify unsettling the animal, which is to say: it is traditional. Working form (Eq. 8.73): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 - k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR17) -- held over t_hold Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Hawk's Lend (N-GR-17): eta_NGR17 is how much of the target's weight the ripple actually addresses, which for a bulky load is never all of it.

[N-GR-18] Mason's Third Hand (Novice, Gravity). Light Load on a stone through the final hand-span of its placement — not the lift, the setting, where fingers would otherwise be. Masons' guilds credit it with more saved hands than any physician, and apprentice it accordingly. Strong (k_strong) — extends Eq. 4.0c. Working form (Eq. 8.74): F_net = m_t * g_local * (1 - k_grav * Fid * eta_NGR18) v_term = sqrt(2 * F_net * h_drop / m_t) Working form of Eq. 4.0b for Mason's Third Hand (N-GR-18): eta_NGR18 is the share of the fall the caster catches, set by how soon the ripple reaches the thing.

[N-ST-03] Edge Hold (Novice, Strong). Seal Bind's boost (N-ST-01) laid along a cutting edge, resisting the rolling and dulling of a day's work. The edge is not sharper — it is merely still sharp at dusk. Harvest crews hire it by the field. Working form (Eq. 8.75): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST03) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Edge Hold (N-ST-03): eta_NST03 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-ST-04] Green Split (Novice, Strong). Brittle Ease (N-ST-02) run down a billet's grain-line before the maul falls. Firewood splits true; knots surrender ungracefully but surrender. The most commercially common strong-force casting in cold country. Working form (Eq. 8.76): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST04) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Green Split (N-ST-04): eta_NST04 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-ST-05] Knot Faith (Novice, Strong). Seal Bind at the crossings of a tied knot — the knot holds against loads that would walk it loose, yet unties by hand when the casting lapses. Riggers value the reversibility over the strength; a fused knot is just a lump. Working form (Eq. 8.77): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST05) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Knot Faith (N-ST-05): eta_NST05 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-ST-06] Patch Press (Novice, Strong). Seal Bind holding a patch to a hull, boot, or bellows seam while proper repair waits for shore, bench, or morning. Explicitly a promise to fix something later — several harbor authorities require patched hulls to carry proof of a standing repair contract for exactly this reason. Working form (Eq. 8.78): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST06) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Patch Press (N-ST-06): eta_NST06 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-ST-07] Chisel's Consent (Novice, Strong). Brittle Ease a finger's width ahead of a chisel line in stone or hardwood. The material parts where asked and nowhere else. Carvers describe the sensation as the workpiece agreeing — the directory records the phrasing because every carving tradition independently arrives at it. Working form (Eq. 8.79): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST07) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Chisel's Consent (N-ST-07): eta_NST07 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-ST-08] Thread Lock (Novice, Strong). Seal Bind at a screw's threads, a peg's seat, an axle pin. Holds against vibration that would back the fastener out; releases to a deliberate hand on the tool. Wainwrights cast it as routinely as they grease. Working form (Eq. 8.80): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST08) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Thread Lock (N-ST-08): eta_NST08 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-ST-09] Shatterguard (Novice, Strong). Eq. 4.0c across a glass vessel, a fired pot, a lens — held for the duration of a transport. A dropped crate still breaks; a jostled one doesn't. Carriers price fragile freight with and without a caster riding along, and the difference is the technique's market value, published quarterly. Working form (Eq. 8.81): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST09) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Shatterguard (N-ST-09): eta_NST09 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-ST-10] Clean Break (Novice, Strong). Brittle Ease at an old, badly-healed fracture so a mender can re-break precisely where intended rather than where the bone prefers. Cast only ever alongside a mender's direct instruction; the technique is Novice, the judgment of where is not, and every guild charter that mentions this entry says so. Working form (Eq. 8.82): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST10) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Clean Break (N-ST-10): eta_NST10 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-ST-11] Miller's Mercy (Novice, Strong). Brittle Ease across grain hulls at the millstone's mouth — flour from less force, less heat, fewer burnt batches. Millers who employ a caster advertise it; customers taste the difference or claim to. Working form (Eq. 8.83): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST11) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Miller's Mercy (N-ST-11): eta_NST11 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-ST-12] Supple Hand (Novice, Strong). Brittle Ease at its gentlest, worked through stiff leather, dried rope, or a rusted hinge's seized grain. Loosens what disuse has hardened without weakening what should hold. The restorer's counterpart to N-ST-01, and cast with the same touch. Working form (Eq. 8.84): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST12) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Supple Hand (N-ST-12): eta_NST12 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-ST-13] Anchor Bite (Novice, Strong). Seal Bind into the soil gripping a stake, piton, or fence post — the ground itself briefly bound around the shaft. Ends, like all of these, when the casting ends; a camp that stands a season is held by dug anchors, not held breath. Working form (Eq. 8.85): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST13) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Anchor Bite (N-ST-13): eta_NST13 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-ST-14] Mortar's Reprieve (Novice, Strong). Seal Bind across frost-cracked mortar or a split lintel, buying a wall the weeks between discovery and repair. Building wardens keep ledgers of standing reprieves precisely because the technique is good enough to invite forgetting — the directory notes, without comment, that every such ledger has at least one entry older than its warden. Working form (Eq. 8.86): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST14) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Mortar's Reprieve (N-ST-14): eta_NST14 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-ST-15] Quarry Line (Novice, Strong). Brittle Ease cast point by point along a scribed line across rock — each point a separate, complete casting, the line parting under wedges where it was eased. A patient Novice splits stone a gang of hammers couldn't; an impatient one learns why the points are cast separately.
