Working form (Eq. 8.87): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 - k_strong * Fid * eta_NST15) -- reverse-sign casting, along the grain Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Quarry Line (N-ST-15): eta_NST15 is how well the weakened line follows the grain rather than crossing it; a good caster scores, a poor one shatters.

[N-ST-16] Barrel True (Novice, Strong). Seal Bind at a hoop's seat while the cooper drives it home, then released — the bind holds the stave-line true during the set, and the finished barrel holds by craft alone. A signature example of aether as a tool of a trade rather than a replacement for it. Working form (Eq. 8.88): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 + k_strong * Fid * eta_NST16) -- over the seam's area A_t only Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Barrel True (N-ST-16): eta_NST16 is the seam's area against the whole object's; the boost is spent on the line that leaks.

[N-ST-17] Wheelwright's Weld (Novice, Strong). Seal Bind clamping a felloe joint or chair joint while glue cures — hours of t_hold at trivial intensity. Workshops schedule these castings the way they schedule the glue, and apprentice casters bill by the drying afternoon. Weak (k_weak) — extends Eq. 4.0d. The couplings here remain, per that equation's write-up, faint by nature at this tier; every entry below is honest about it. Working form (Eq. 8.89): E_bind_eff = E_bind * (1 + k_strong * Fid * eta_NST17) -- over the seam's area A_t only Working form of Eq. 4.0c for Wheelwright's Weld (N-ST-17): eta_NST17 is the seam's area against the whole object's; the boost is spent on the line that leaks.

[N-WK-03] Slow Larder (Novice, Weak). Eq. 4.0d as a reverse-sign casting — the decay nudge run downward, slowing spoilage by a margin measured in extra days, not seasons. The pantry-scale ancestor of what Quiet Mend (AD-05) blends and Eq. 4.19 (s = -1) perfects; the family resemblance is the standard lecture example for how one channel deepens across four tiers. Working form (Eq. 8.90): Gamma_eff = Gamma_0 * (1 - k_weak * Fid * eta_NWK03) -- reverse-sign casting t_spoil = t_spoil_0 * Gamma_0 / Gamma_eff Working form of Eq. 4.0d for Slow Larder (N-WK-03): eta_NWK03 is how much of the target's decay the nudge can reach; a whole cask answers less than a single seal.

[N-WK-04] Hearthstone (Novice, Weak). A smooth stone nudged to a faint, steady warmth (Eq. 4.0d held low), wrapped in flannel at the foot of a bed. Output a candle would mock; comfort a candle can't match, since it cannot gutter, tip, or burn a sleeping child. The signature domestic casting of weak-force households. Working form (Eq. 8.91): Gamma_eff = Gamma_0 * (1 + k_weak * Fid * eta_NWK04) t_cure = t_cure_0 * Gamma_0 / Gamma_eff Working form of Eq. 4.0d for Hearthstone (N-WK-04): eta_NWK04 is how much of the cure's slow chemistry answers to the nudge; some processes barely do, and the entry says so.

[N-WK-05] Assayer's Glow (Novice, Weak). Eq. 4.0d cast across a spread of crushed ore — fractions bearing trace unstable material answer with a faint luminescence, and the assayer reads the sparkle like a map. One of the few Novice techniques that meaningfully prospects, and the historical reason weak-force casters cluster in mining towns. Working form (Eq. 8.92): Gamma_eff = Gamma_0 * (1 + k_weak * Fid * eta_NWK05) t_cure = t_cure_0 * Gamma_0 / Gamma_eff Working form of Eq. 4.0d for Assayer's Glow (N-WK-05): eta_NWK05 is how much of the cure's slow chemistry answers to the nudge; some processes barely do, and the entry says so.

[N-WK-06] Compost Quicken (Novice, Weak). Quick Ripen's logic (N-WK-01) turned on a heap rather than an orchard row — decomposition already underway, nudged. A season's soil in most of one. Estate gardeners consider it beneath discussion and cast it weekly. Working form (Eq. 8.93): Gamma_eff = Gamma_0 * (1 + k_weak * Fid * eta_NWK06) t_cure = t_cure_0 * Gamma_0 / Gamma_eff Working form of Eq. 4.0d for Compost Quicken (N-WK-06): eta_NWK06 is how much of the cure's slow chemistry answers to the nudge; some processes barely do, and the entry says so.

[N-WK-07] Mourner's Candle (Novice, Weak). Faint Ward-Light (N-WK-02) formalized for a vigil: one caster, one night, one steady glow that cannot blow out. Several funerary traditions hold that the light must be held, not merely lit — the point being the attendance, which a lamp cannot offer. Working form (Eq. 8.94): Gamma_eff = Gamma_0 * (1 + k_weak * Fid * eta_NWK07) P_out = Gamma_eff * E_per_decay * N_unstable -- held over t_hold; faint by nature Working form of Eq. 4.0d for Mourner's Candle (N-WK-07): eta_NWK07 is how much of the trace unstable material in the target is actually within reach of the nudge.

[N-WK-08] Deep Mark (Novice, Weak). Ward-light worked into mineral-rich cave paint, leaving marks that answer a later caster's nudge with a soft glow. Cavers' guilds blaze routes in it; the marks outlast the guilds, and mapping dead guilds' marks is its own small profession. Working form (Eq. 8.95): Gamma_eff = Gamma_0 * (1 + k_weak * Fid * eta_NWK08) P_out = Gamma_eff * E_per_decay * N_unstable -- as warmth; held at duty D_cycle Working form of Eq. 4.0d for Deep Mark (N-WK-08): eta_NWK08 is how much of the faint radiant output is kept as warmth rather than lost as glow.

[N-WK-09] Leak Finder (Novice, Weak). A trace of nudge-responsive mineral salt fed into a water line or millrace, then followed by its faint glow to wherever the flow escapes. Aqueduct wardens' standard diagnostic, and the technique most often cited when someone argues weak-force casting is underrated. Working form (Eq. 8.96): Gamma_eff = Gamma_0 * (1 + k_weak * Fid * eta_NWK09) t_cure = t_cure_0 * Gamma_0 / Gamma_eff Working form of Eq. 4.0d for Leak Finder (N-WK-09): eta_NWK09 is how much of the cure's slow chemistry answers to the nudge; some processes barely do, and the entry says so.

[N-WK-10] Long Watch (Novice, Weak). Faint Ward-Light rebalanced for duration over brightness — output near the resolution threshold (Eq. 3.3), hold measured in full nights. The endurance benchmark for weak-force Novices, as Sun's Patience (N-EM-22) is for their EM peers. Working form (Eq. 8.97): Gamma_eff = Gamma_0 * (1 + k_weak * Fid * eta_NWK10) t_cure = t_cure_0 * Gamma_0 / Gamma_eff Working form of Eq. 4.0d for Long Watch (N-WK-10): eta_NWK10 is how much of the cure's slow chemistry answers to the nudge; some processes barely do, and the entry says so.

[N-WK-11] Salamander's Breath (Novice, Weak). Hearthstone's warmth cast directly into a bedroll, boot, or glove for the minutes it takes to stop shivering. Border sentries call the technique by this name in six languages; the directory declines to rule on which came first. Working form (Eq. 8.98): Gamma_eff = Gamma_0 * (1 + k_weak * Fid * eta_NWK11) t_cure = t_cure_0 * Gamma_0 / Gamma_eff Working form of Eq. 4.0d for Salamander's Breath (N-WK-11): eta_NWK11 is how much of the cure's slow chemistry answers to the nudge; some processes barely do, and the entry says so.

[N-WK-12] Miller's Clock (Novice, Weak). A pinch of nudge-responsive salt in a sealed vial, its glow decaying at a known rate once nudged — a crude, unstealable timer for processes that outlast attention: proofing dough, steeping dye, a rented hour. Accurate to about a tenth; disputed at the margins in every market that uses it. Working form (Eq. 8.99): Gamma_eff = Gamma_0 * (1 + k_weak * Fid * eta_NWK12) P_out = Gamma_eff * E_per_decay * N_unstable -- held over t_hold; faint by nature Working form of Eq. 4.0d for Miller's Clock (N-WK-12): eta_NWK12 is how much of the trace unstable material in the target is actually within reach of the nudge.

[J-08] Harvest Round (Journeyman). N-ST-03 on the scythe at dawn, N-EM-22 on the racks at noon. A single caster carries a farm's cutting and drying through harvest by never once trying to do both at once. Working form (Eq. 8.100): X_seq(t) = X_NST03(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NEM22(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Harvest Round (J-08): the two windows carry N-ST-03 and N-EM-22; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-09] Ferryman's Habit (Journeyman). N-GR-07 in the crossing, N-GR-16 at the landing, switched as the deck empties. Same force, two closed forms — the pairing that most often teaches a Journeyman that Eq. 4.13 doesn't care whether the two windows share a k_f. Working form (Eq. 8.101): X_seq(t) = X_NGR07(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NGR16(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Ferryman's Habit (J-09): the two windows carry N-GR-07 and N-GR-16; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-10] Surgeon's Table (Journeyman). N-GR-04 on the instrument, then N-ST-10 at the mender's word, never overlapping — the hand must be steady before the bone is eased, and the sequence is legally fixed in three guild charters. Working form (Eq. 8.102): X_seq(t) = X_NGR04(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NST10(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Surgeon's Table (J-10): the two windows carry N-GR-04 and N-ST-10; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-11] Glazier's Morning (Journeyman). N-EM-19 to sketch the cut, N-ST-02 to make it. Frost line, then brittle line, in strict order; reversing them ruins the pane and is the trade's standard joke about impatient apprentices. Working form (Eq. 8.103): X_seq(t) = X_NEM19(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NST02(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Glazier's Morning (J-11): the two windows carry N-EM-19 and N-ST-02; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-12] Winter Doorstep (Journeyman). N-EM-20 held indoors or N-WK-04 sent to the beds, chosen nightly by fuel, weather, and who's home. A householder's version of J-03's either/or discipline. Working form (Eq. 8.104): X_seq(t) = X_NEM20(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NWK04(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Winter Doorstep (J-12): the two windows carry N-EM-20 and N-WK-04; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-13] Prospector's Walk (Journeyman). N-WK-05 across the spread, then N-ST-15 along the seam it reveals. Read, then split; the assay window closes before the quarry window opens. Working form (Eq. 8.105): X_seq(t) = X_NWK05(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NST15(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Prospector's Walk (J-13): the two windows carry N-WK-05 and N-ST-15; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-14] Dockmaster's Pair (Journeyman). N-GR-06 over the swinging crate, N-ST-09 on the fragile one — never both on one load, because a load that needs both needs a better crane. Working form (Eq. 8.106): X_seq(t) = X_NGR06(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NST09(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Dockmaster's Pair (J-14): the two windows carry N-GR-06 and N-ST-09; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-15] Night Fisher (Journeyman). N-EM-24 to raise the shoal, N-GR-13 to lay the net's throw long. Lure, then cast; the lure dies the moment the net flies, which the fish appear not to have learned in several centuries. Working form (Eq. 8.107): X_seq(t) = X_NEM24(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NGR13(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Night Fisher (J-15): the two windows carry N-EM-24 and N-GR-13; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-16] Courier's Descent (Journeyman). N-GR-08 up the ridge, N-GR-01 down the scarp. The mountain courier's canonical pair, and the worked example most curricula use for drilling tau_switch under fatigue. Working form (Eq. 8.108): X_seq(t) = X_NGR08(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NGR01(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Courier's Descent (J-16): the two windows carry N-GR-08 and N-GR-01; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-17] Physician's Round (Journeyman). N-EM-14 to read the fever, N-EM-02 to ease it. Gauge, then chill, in alternation through the night — a discipline built on never trusting the last reading through the current casting. Working form (Eq. 8.109): X_seq(t) = X_NEM14(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NEM02(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Physician's Round (J-17): the two windows carry N-EM-14 and N-EM-02; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-18] Archivist's Bench (Journeyman). N-EM-11 across the folio, then N-ST-12 through its cracked spine. Clean, then soften. The reverse order grinds loosened grit into the leather, a mistake each archivist is permitted exactly once. Working form (Eq. 8.110): X_seq(t) = X_NEM11(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NST12(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Archivist's Bench (J-18): the two windows carry N-EM-11 and N-ST-12; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-19] Stable Fire Drill (Journeyman). N-EM-15 on the lamp, N-GR-14 across the spooked animal. Snuff, then settle. Written into stable standing orders in most walled towns, in that order, in large letters. Working form (Eq. 8.111): X_seq(t) = X_NEM15(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NGR14(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Stable Fire Drill (J-19): the two windows carry N-EM-15 and N-GR-14; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-20] Wall Warden's Round (Journeyman). N-ST-14 on the crack at morning, N-WK-09 through the cistern line at noon. The maintenance Journeyman's archetype: two small competences, held honestly apart, worth more than either doubled. Working form (Eq. 8.112): X_seq(t) = X_NST14(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NWK09(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Wall Warden's Round (J-20): the two windows carry N-ST-14 and N-WK-09; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-21] Smith's Apprentice Round (Journeyman). N-EM-13 to wake the forge, N-GR-12 to pin the work. The pairing traditionally assigned the year before Two-Handed Smith (J-05), and the reason that year exists. Working form (Eq. 8.113): X_seq(t) = X_NEM13(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NGR12(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Smith's Apprentice Round (J-21): the two windows carry N-EM-13 and N-GR-12; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-22] Lens-Grinder's Sequence (Journeyman). N-ST-09 while the blank travels, N-EM-19 to mark the grind. Guard window closed, mark window opened, no overlap — an heirloom sequence in workshops that cannot afford one dropped blank. Working form (Eq. 8.114): X_seq(t) = X_NST09(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NEM19(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Lens-Grinder's Sequence (J-22): the two windows carry N-ST-09 and N-EM-19; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-23] Vintner's Cellar Round (Journeyman). N-WK-06 at the press-waste heap, N-WK-03 over the must. Hasten one decay, slow another, same force, opposite signs, and a cellar-master's entire reputation living in never confusing the targets. Working form (Eq. 8.115): X_seq(t) = X_NWK06(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NWK03(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Vintner's Cellar Round (J-23): the two windows carry N-WK-06 and N-WK-03; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-24] Siege Porter (Journeyman). N-GR-18 setting the stone, N-ST-13 binding the stake-line. The field-works pairing; drilled to a called cadence so a wall crew's several Journeymen switch on the same beat. Working form (Eq. 8.116): X_seq(t) = X_NGR18(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NST13(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Siege Porter (J-24): the two windows carry N-GR-18 and N-ST-13; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-25] Beacon Chain (Journeyman). N-EM-07 by day or N-EM-21 by night, chosen by light and weather — J-06's relay discipline with the choice itself formalized as the skill. Working form (Eq. 8.117): X_seq(t) = X_NEM07(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NEM21(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Beacon Chain (J-25): the two windows carry N-EM-07 and N-EM-21; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-26] Falconer's Launch (Journeyman). N-GR-17 off the glove, then N-EM-24 held far afield to mark the lure point. Bird lightened, then light raised; the windows must not touch or the bird chases the wrong brightness. Working form (Eq. 8.118): X_seq(t) = X_NGR17(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NEM24(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Falconer's Launch (J-26): the two windows carry N-GR-17 and N-EM-24; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-27] Ropewalk Round (Journeyman). N-ST-05 proving the knots, N-ST-01 sealing the whipped ends. A rigger's same-force pair, examined annually in every harbor that licenses one. Working form (Eq. 8.119): X_seq(t) = X_NST05(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NST01(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Ropewalk Round (J-27): the two windows carry N-ST-05 and N-ST-01; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-28] Icefield Crossing (Journeyman). N-GR-02 on the crosser's own steps, N-GR-06 held ready over the sledge. The second window opens only if the first fails — a contingency pairing, and most curricula's first example of holding a casting in reserve rather than in effect. Working form (Eq. 8.120): X_seq(t) = X_NGR02(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NGR06(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Icefield Crossing (J-28): the two windows carry N-GR-02 and N-GR-06; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-29] Kiln Watch (Journeyman). N-EM-06 through the long soak, N-EM-14 at the hour-marks. Hold, gauge, hold again; the gauge pulse cannot read truly while the heating window is open, which is the whole lesson. Working form (Eq. 8.121): X_seq(t) = X_NEM06(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NEM14(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Kiln Watch (J-29): the two windows carry N-EM-06 and N-EM-14; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-30] Orchard Round (Journeyman). N-WK-01 along the early rows, N-GR-13 lofting sacks to the cart. The picking crew's pairing, unremarkable everywhere fruit is grown, which is the point of cataloguing it. Working form (Eq. 8.122): X_seq(t) = X_NWK01(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NGR13(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Orchard Round (J-30): the two windows carry N-WK-01 and N-GR-13; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-31] Tinker's Call (Journeyman). N-EM-18 to ring ahead, N-GR-10 at the well when the work is watering. An itinerant's pairing chosen for breadth of custom rather than depth of either. Working form (Eq. 8.123): X_seq(t) = X_NEM18(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NGR10(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Tinker's Call (J-31): the two windows carry N-EM-18 and N-GR-10; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-32] Quarry Foreman's Day (Journeyman). N-ST-15 along the line, then N-GR-15's sectional lightening as the block walks the ramp. Split window closed before lift window opens; the trade's oldest safety verse says so in rhyme. Working form (Eq. 8.124): X_seq(t) = X_NST15(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NGR15(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Quarry Foreman's Day (J-32): the two windows carry N-ST-15 and N-GR-15; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-33] Night Nurse's Round (Journeyman). N-WK-04 to the beds, N-WK-10 at the door. Warmth, then watch-light, resumed in alternation through the dark — the humblest entry in this directory's Journeyman tier and, by any honest count of castings performed, its most practiced. Working form (Eq. 8.125): X_seq(t) = X_NWK04(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NWK10(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Night Nurse's Round (J-33): the two windows carry N-WK-04 and N-WK-10; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-34] Carpenter's Close (Journeyman). N-ST-17 clamping the joint, then N-ST-08 locking the pegs once dry. Same force, sequential by necessity: the glue's schedule, not the caster's, sets tau_switch's floor — a favorite exam question. Working form (Eq. 8.126): X_seq(t) = X_NST17(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NST08(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Carpenter's Close (J-34): the two windows carry N-ST-17 and N-ST-08; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-35] Harbor Light Relay (Journeyman). N-EM-03 in the tower or N-WK-02 on the buoy-line, chosen by fog. The keeper's either/or; on the worst nights the choice reverses hourly, and the log of choices is the keeper's real deliverable. Working form (Eq. 8.127): X_seq(t) = X_NEM03(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NWK02(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Harbor Light Relay (J-35): the two windows carry N-EM-03 and N-WK-02; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-36] Drover's Ford (Journeyman). N-GR-16 while wading the herd, N-EM-12 strung at the far bank's pen. Cross, then fence. Held apart because a spark anywhere near a mid-river herd is a lesson no drover needs twice. Working form (Eq. 8.128): X_seq(t) = X_NGR16(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NEM12(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Drover's Ford (J-36): the two windows carry N-GR-16 and N-EM-12; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-37] Engraver's Sitting (Journeyman). N-GR-04 on the burin, N-EM-25 around the plate. Steady the hand, quiet the field, in alternation as the work demands — a pairing whose customers, like Quiet Coil's, are mostly other casters. Working form (Eq. 8.129): X_seq(t) = X_NGR04(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NEM25(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Engraver's Sitting (J-37): the two windows carry N-GR-04 and N-EM-25; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-38] Storm Prep Round (Journeyman). N-ST-06 over the seams, N-GR-11 to trim her as the crew works. The pre-gale checklist pairing; every harbor's version differs and every harbor is certain theirs is canonical. Working form (Eq. 8.130): X_seq(t) = X_NST06(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NGR11(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Storm Prep Round (J-38): the two windows carry N-ST-06 and N-GR-11; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-39] Assay Office Sequence (Journeyman). N-WK-05 across the sample, N-EM-14 into the suspect fraction. Glow to find it, pulse to weigh its wetness — two reads in sequence, the directory's cleanest example that Journeyman discipline governs information-gathering castings as strictly as forceful ones. Working form (Eq. 8.131): X_seq(t) = X_NWK05(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NEM14(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Assay Office Sequence (J-39): the two windows carry N-WK-05 and N-EM-14; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-40] Bellringer's Feint (Journeyman). N-EM-18 to sound the far bell, then N-GR-01 stepping off the tower stair's worn edge. A sexton's pairing in old towers; drilled, like Bladeline Feint (J-07), to the smallest tau_switch its holder can survive being wrong about. Working form (Eq. 8.132): X_seq(t) = X_NEM18(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NGR01(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Bellringer's Feint (J-40): the two windows carry N-EM-18 and N-GR-01; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-41] Foundling's Kit (Journeyman). N-EM-01 or N-WK-11, chosen by what the night needs lit or warmed. The classic first pairing of self-taught casters, catalogued precisely because it appears independently, everywhere, in exactly this form. Working form (Eq. 8.133): X_seq(t) = X_NEM01(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NWK11(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Foundling's Kit (J-41): the two windows carry N-EM-01 and N-WK-11; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-42] Paper-Maker's Day (Journeyman). N-EM-22 over the drying felts, N-ST-12 through yesterday's brittle sheets. Dry the new, ease the old; the windows are half a workshop apart and still, formally, disjoint. Working form (Eq. 8.134): X_seq(t) = X_NEM22(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NST12(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Paper-Maker's Day (J-42): the two windows carry N-EM-22 and N-ST-12; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-43] Sapper's Discipline (Journeyman). N-ST-02 at the marked stone, N-EM-05 held between castings, listening for another crew's work through the wall. Ease, then listen; the passive read costs nothing (Eq. 4.0e) but attention, and the discipline of actually stopping to spend it is the entry. Working form (Eq. 8.135): X_seq(t) = X_NST02(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NEM05(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Sapper's Discipline (J-43): the two windows carry N-ST-02 and N-EM-05; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-44] Ostler's Evening (Journeyman). N-GR-14 across the tired animal, N-WK-04 in its water trough against the frost. The pairing that keeps coaching inns' beasts sound through winter, and ostlers' guilds in dispute with casters' guilds over whose members it belongs to. Working form (Eq. 8.136): X_seq(t) = X_NGR14(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NWK04(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Ostler's Evening (J-44): the two windows carry N-GR-14 and N-WK-04; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-45] Toll Keeper's Test (Journeyman). N-EM-14's pulse into a suspect cask, then N-ST-01 re-sealing the tap-hole. Excise work: read, then reseal, leaving no sign — the directory notes that both windows also open in the smuggler's version, in the other order. Working form (Eq. 8.137): X_seq(t) = X_NEM14(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NST01(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Toll Keeper's Test (J-45): the two windows carry N-EM-14 and N-ST-01; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-46] Winter Mason's Pair (Journeyman). N-EM-20 held around the curing mortar, N-ST-14 across yesterday's frost damage. Warm the new work, hold the old; cold-country building seasons are two castings longer than they used to be. Working form (Eq. 8.138): X_seq(t) = X_NEM20(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NST14(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Winter Mason's Pair (J-46): the two windows carry N-EM-20 and N-ST-14; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[J-47] Rescue Line (Journeyman). N-GR-13 sending the rope long, then N-GR-16 as the hauler sets their feet. Throw light, stand heavy — drilled by every river-rescue watch to a called two-beat, because in the water between the two windows is somebody's neighbor. Working form (Eq. 8.139): X_seq(t) = X_NGR13(t) * Win_1(t) + X_NGR16(t) * Win_2(t) Win_1(t) . Win_2(t) = 0 t_round = N_rep * (w_1 + w_2) + (2 * N_rep - 1) * tau_switch Working form of Eq. 4.13 for Rescue Line (J-47): the two windows carry N-GR-13 and N-GR-16; the round is timed by tau_switch alone.

[AD-07] Annealing Breath (Adept, EM+Strong). Heat and a gentle cohesion ease blended, walking a stressed metal's grain back to softness in one pass. Flash-Forge's mirror image: where AD-01 joins, this relaxes. Toolmakers who hold both describe them as one technique with a sign choice. Working form (Eq. 8.140): X_combo = k_EM * k_strong * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Strong) * eta_AD07 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Annealing Breath (AD-07), on the EM + Strong pair: eta_AD07 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-08] Glasswright's Kiss (Adept, EM+Strong). Localized heat and a cohesion boost held at a crack's tip, healing a glass flaw without slumping the pane. The blend exists because sequential casting fails here: heat alone spreads the crack in the gap before a second casting could bind it — tau_switch is precisely the technique's enemy, which makes it the standard demonstration that Adept tier is a different kind of casting, not a faster Journeyman. Working form (Eq. 8.141): X_combo = k_EM * k_strong * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Strong) * eta_AD08 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Glasswright's Kiss (AD-08), on the EM + Strong pair: eta_AD08 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-09] Coldwright's Temper (Adept, EM+Strong). Deep chill (Eq. 4.0a reversed) blended with a cohesion boost, setting a hardened edge without a quench-bath's warp. Smithing traditions that hold AD-01 and AD-09 both speak of fire-write and frost-write as the pair's two hands. Working form (Eq. 8.142): X_combo = k_EM * k_strong * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Strong) * eta_AD09 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Coldwright's Temper (AD-09), on the EM + Strong pair: eta_AD09 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-10] Breachwright's Answer (Adept, EM+Strong). Heat and brittleness driven together into a lock, hinge, or grate: the metal is hot and frangible in the same instant, and one blow does the rest. The pair's siege expression, licensed accordingly almost everywhere. Working form (Eq. 8.143): X_combo = k_EM * k_strong * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Strong) * eta_AD10 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Breachwright's Answer (AD-10), on the EM + Strong pair: eta_AD10 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-11] Solder Line (Adept, EM+Strong). Arc Splice's heat blended with Seal Bind's grip, running a continuous sealed seam along a boiler course or still-pipe in one inscription. The industrial workhorse of this pair; entire manufactories are laid out around how far one Adept can walk a seam before Fid^2 sags. Working form (Eq. 8.144): X_combo = k_EM * k_strong * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Strong) * eta_AD11 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Solder Line (AD-11), on the EM + Strong pair: eta_AD11 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-12] Cooper's Furnace (Adept, EM+Strong). Steam-bending heat and a grain-line cohesion ease blended along a stave or rib, curving seasoned wood in one dry pass with no steam box and no springback. The shipwright's and cooper's shared prize; yards that retain a holder bend frames to curves their rivals' molds cannot draw. (EM + Gravity — the Storm-Step pair, AD-02) Working form (Eq. 8.145): X_combo = k_EM * k_strong * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Strong) * eta_AD12 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Cooper's Furnace (AD-12), on the EM + Strong pair: eta_AD12 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-13] Crane Whisper (Adept, EM+Gravity). A signal pulse and a lightening blended so the load lightens on the signal, in the same casting, across a work yard. What J-14 does with two windows, one Adept does with none; dock guilds bill the difference by the hour. Working form (Eq. 8.146): X_combo = k_EM * k_gravity * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Gravity) * eta_AD13 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Crane Whisper (AD-13), on the EM + Gravity pair: eta_AD13 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-14] Beacon Vault (Adept, EM+Gravity). Storm-Step's leap blended with Mirror Flash's pulse: the courier's arrival is the signal. Border relays built around one Adept replace a tower's worth of Journeyman watchers, which is why border lords count Adepts the way they count cannon. Working form (Eq. 8.147): X_combo = k_EM * k_gravity * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Gravity) * eta_AD14 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Beacon Vault (AD-14), on the EM + Gravity pair: eta_AD14 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-15] Lightning Draw (Adept, EM+Gravity). A discharge blended with a lateral pull on the discharge path itself, bending a spark around cover to a target the caster cannot see straight. The duel-legal ceiling of this pair in most codes; the duel-illegal extensions are the same casting with worse intentions. Working form (Eq. 8.148): X_combo = k_EM * k_gravity * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Gravity) * eta_AD15 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Lightning Draw (AD-15), on the EM + Gravity pair: eta_AD15 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-16] Feather Barrage (Adept, EM+Gravity). Thrown objects lightened in flight and given a static crackle that spooks and scatters — a crowd-control blend built to end brawls without ending brawlers. City watches teach it as their signature Adept technique; city watchmen mostly never make Adept, which keeps its holders employed. Working form (Eq. 8.149): X_combo = k_EM * k_gravity * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Gravity) * eta_AD16 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Feather Barrage (AD-16), on the EM + Gravity pair: eta_AD16 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-17] Lampfall (Adept, EM+Gravity). A hovering glow-point lowered smoothly down a shaft ahead of the descending crew, light and lift as one held blend. Mine rescue's standard-bearer technique, and the entry most often cited when a guild argues an Adept's wage. Working form (Eq. 8.150): X_combo = k_EM * k_gravity * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Gravity) * eta_AD17 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Lampfall (AD-17), on the EM + Gravity pair: eta_AD17 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-18] Stormglass Reading (Adept, EM+Gravity). A diffuse static read and a fine sounding-pull blended across the sky's near column: pressure, charge, and the weight of coming weather from one held casting. The pair's quiet scholarly face; harbor pilots trust a holder's morning over any instrument they own, and say so in their logs. (EM + Weak — the Cinder-Fall pair, AD-03) Working form (Eq. 8.151): X_combo = k_EM * k_gravity * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Gravity) * eta_AD18 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Stormglass Reading (AD-18), on the EM + Gravity pair: eta_AD18 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-19] Forge From Nothing (Adept, EM+Weak). Cinder-Fall pushed to its working limit: a self-feeding heat sustained on fuel so poor it barely deserves the name — wet peat, green wood, bilge scrap. Expedition quartermasters rank it above any weapon this pair offers, and the directory declines to argue. Working form (Eq. 8.152): X_combo = k_EM * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Weak) * eta_AD19 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Forge From Nothing (AD-19), on the EM + Weak pair: eta_AD19 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-20] Watchman's Dawn (Adept, EM+Weak). Ward-light's steadiness blended with lamplight's brightness: a glow that cannot gutter and genuinely lights the yard. The night-watch blend that retires J-35's either/or, in the towns that can hire it. Working form (Eq. 8.153): X_combo = k_EM * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Weak) * eta_AD20 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Watchman's Dawn (AD-20), on the EM + Weak pair: eta_AD20 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-21] Assayer's Lens (Adept, EM+Weak). The decay-glow read and a calibrated heat pulse blended into one probing casting: composition and wetness from a single touch. Turns N-WK-05 and N-EM-14's two windows (J-39) into one instrument; mints and mine offices treat holders as senior staff on arrival. Working form (Eq. 8.154): X_combo = k_EM * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Weak) * eta_AD21 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Assayer's Lens (AD-21), on the EM + Weak pair: eta_AD21 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-22] Slow Match (Adept, EM+Weak). A heat point and a decay nudge blended into a self-timing ignition — a fire that starts later, by a chosen interval, with no fuse to see or cut. Sappers' guilds keep its deeper calibrations off the open directory, and this entry respects that. Working form (Eq. 8.155): X_combo = k_EM * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Weak) * eta_AD22 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Slow Match (AD-22), on the EM + Weak pair: eta_AD22 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-23] Kilnless Fire-Gilding (Adept, EM+Weak). A heat gradient and a decay nudge blended through a glaze or gilt layer, curing in minutes what a kiln cures in a day, with no kiln to crack the piece. Restorers' workshops guard their holders jealously; AR-27's porcelain state guards its own more jealously still. Working form (Eq. 8.156): X_combo = k_EM * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Weak) * eta_AD23 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Kilnless Fire-Gilding (AD-23), on the EM + Weak pair: eta_AD23 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-24] Hearth Eternal (Adept, EM+Weak). Cinder-Fall's self-feeding logic inverted into pure endurance: a banked civic fire blended to draw so little that one charge of fuel warms a hall through a winter's siege. The blend behind three cities' famous "undying" hearths — undying, the directory notes, in exact proportion to their Adepts' renewal calendars. (Gravity + Strong — the Sunder Weight pair, AD-04) Working form (Eq. 8.157): X_combo = k_EM * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(EM, Weak) * eta_AD24 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Hearth Eternal (AD-24), on the EM + Weak pair: eta_AD24 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-25] Mason's Miracle (Adept, Gravity+Strong). A stone lightened and cohesion-boosted through placement: half its weight and twice its patience with handling, in one blend. What N-GR-18 and N-ST-09 do apart, this does whole; cathedral works measure their schedules in how many holders of it they can retain. Working form (Eq. 8.158): X_combo = k_gravity * k_strong * Fid^2 * Chi(Gravity, Strong) * eta_AD25 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Mason's Miracle (AD-25), on the Gravity + Strong pair: eta_AD25 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-26] Controlled Fall (Adept, Gravity+Strong). Sunder Weight's demolition blend refined for direction: the target made heavier and selectively brittle so it fails along a chosen line and drops where told. The difference between demolition and catastrophe, per every guild examiner's opening lecture. Working form (Eq. 8.159): X_combo = k_gravity * k_strong * Fid^2 * Chi(Gravity, Strong) * eta_AD26 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Controlled Fall (AD-26), on the Gravity + Strong pair: eta_AD26 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-27] Bulwark Set (Adept, Gravity+Strong). A barricade's timbers weighted and bound in one casting — heavier to move, harder to break, for as long as the Adept holds. Siege defense's mirror to AD-10; fortress rosters list holders of both under one heading: gatewrights. Working form (Eq. 8.160): X_combo = k_gravity * k_strong * Fid^2 * Chi(Gravity, Strong) * eta_AD27 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Bulwark Set (AD-27), on the Gravity + Strong pair: eta_AD27 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-28] Wrecker's Mercy (Adept, Gravity+Strong). A collapsing structure's fragments lightened and toughened mid-fall, so what lands, lands soft and whole. The rescue blend of a demolition pair — the directory's standing example that a pair's moral character belongs to its caster, not its Chi. Working form (Eq. 8.161): X_combo = k_gravity * k_strong * Fid^2 * Chi(Gravity, Strong) * eta_AD28 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Wrecker's Mercy (AD-28), on the Gravity + Strong pair: eta_AD28 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-29] Anchor Absolute (Adept, Gravity+Strong). A ship's anchor weighted and its cable's grip bound as one blend through a blow. Harbormasters in storm latitudes retain one Adept for this the way they retain one pilot, and for the same nights. Working form (Eq. 8.162): X_combo = k_gravity * k_strong * Fid^2 * Chi(Gravity, Strong) * eta_AD29 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Anchor Absolute (AD-29), on the Gravity + Strong pair: eta_AD29 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-30] Avalanche Writ (Adept, Gravity+Strong). A loaded slope's snowpack made locally heavier and more frangible on a chosen line, releasing the slide at a chosen hour onto an emptied path. Sunder Weight turned to prevention; high-country districts post the writ's schedule beside the church door, and attendance at both is customary. (Strong + Weak — the Quiet Mend pair, AD-05) Working form (Eq. 8.163): X_combo = k_gravity * k_strong * Fid^2 * Chi(Gravity, Strong) * eta_AD30 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Avalanche Writ (AD-30), on the Gravity + Strong pair: eta_AD30 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-31] Reliquary Seal (Adept, Strong+Weak). Quiet Mend deepened to institutional scale: an object's binds boosted and its decay slowed as one standing blend, renewed on a calendar. Archives and reliquaries keep seal-books recording each renewal — the humble ancestor, several lecturers note, of the recertification ledgers Legend tier lives by (Eq. 4.23). Working form (Eq. 8.164): X_combo = k_strong * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(Strong, Weak) * eta_AD31 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Reliquary Seal (AD-31), on the Strong + Weak pair: eta_AD31 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-32] Surgeon's Hold (Adept, Strong+Weak). Tissue's cohesion boosted and its decay arrested together at a wound too grave to close — a blend that buys hours at the edge of what Novice and Journeyman menders can buy at all. Not healing: time. Every tradition that holds it says those words in its oath. Working form (Eq. 8.165): X_combo = k_strong * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(Strong, Weak) * eta_AD32 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Surgeon's Hold (AD-32), on the Strong + Weak pair: eta_AD32 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-33] Ship-Biscuit Blessing (Adept, Strong+Weak). Provisions' binds toughened and spoilage slowed in one hold-wide casting before a long passage. Unglamorous even by this pair's standards, and the blend most often named in shipping contracts by its plain effect: the cargo arrives. Working form (Eq. 8.166): X_combo = k_strong * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(Strong, Weak) * eta_AD33 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Ship-Biscuit Blessing (AD-33), on the Strong + Weak pair: eta_AD33 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-34] Rot-Fence (Adept, Strong+Weak). The pair run in opposed signs: decay hastened in a blighted limb of an orchard row while the healthy wood's binds are boosted against its spread. The blend's judgment burden — where the fence falls — is the entry's real difficulty, and the reason orchard wardens who hold it sit on rural courts. Working form (Eq. 8.167): X_combo = k_strong * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(Strong, Weak) * eta_AD34 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Rot-Fence (AD-34), on the Strong + Weak pair: eta_AD34 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-35] Tanner's Secret (Adept, Strong+Weak). A hide's decay pathway nudged while its fiber binds are held — controlled cure in days, supple as months. The trade blend AR-04's eigenvector work resembles from the outside; the two are routinely confused, and both trades profit from the confusion. Working form (Eq. 8.168): X_combo = k_strong * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(Strong, Weak) * eta_AD35 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Tanner's Secret (AD-35), on the Strong + Weak pair: eta_AD35 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-36] Seed Writ (Adept, Strong+Weak). Seed-stock's coats bind-boosted while dormancy's slow decay is arrested, one granary-blessing casting holding a district's next planting viable across a failed year. AD-33's logic pointed at the year after this one; famine-country traditions rank its holders above physicians, and physicians there agree. (Gravity + Weak — the Grave Lantern pair, AD-06) Working form (Eq. 8.169): X_combo = k_strong * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(Strong, Weak) * eta_AD36 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Seed Writ (AD-36), on the Strong + Weak pair: eta_AD36 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-37] Vigil Bier (Adept, Gravity+Weak). Grave Lantern held at procession scale: the bier lightened to its bearers and lit with a steady ward-glow across the whole rite. The ceremonial pair's ceremonial deepening; several traditions hold that the casting must be one Adept's alone, unrelieved, and that the fatigue is part of the observance. Working form (Eq. 8.170): X_combo = k_gravity * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(Gravity, Weak) * eta_AD37 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Vigil Bier (AD-37), on the Gravity + Weak pair: eta_AD37 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-38] Deep Sounding (Adept, Gravity+Weak). A glow-traced weight lowered on a blended casting down a shaft, well, or wreck — depth read from the descent, condition from the glow's return. The surveyor's expression of a funerary pair, and proof, cited in every lecture on this pair, that no pair is only what its signature suggests. Working form (Eq. 8.171): X_combo = k_gravity * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(Gravity, Weak) * eta_AD38 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Deep Sounding (AD-38), on the Gravity + Weak pair: eta_AD38 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-39] Beacon Buoy (Adept, Gravity+Weak). A marker held just off true rest and lit with unquenchable ward-light, riding a reef or bar through weather that would drown any lamp. Coastal charities fund holders of this blend the way inland towns fund bridges. Working form (Eq. 8.172): X_combo = k_gravity * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(Gravity, Weak) * eta_AD39 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Beacon Buoy (AD-39), on the Gravity + Weak pair: eta_AD39 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AD-40] Lightened Watch (Adept, Gravity+Weak). A sentry's own body faintly lightened and faintly lit — steps silent on old floors, presence marked to allies by a glow only Ripple Sense reads at range. The pair's one martial expression, favored by honest garrisons and dishonest guests in exactly equal measure. Working form (Eq. 8.173): X_combo = k_gravity * k_weak * Fid^2 * Chi(Gravity, Weak) * eta_AD40 * dAe_local Working form of Eq. 4.15 for Lightened Watch (AD-40), on the Gravity + Weak pair: eta_AD40 is how much of the blended distortion reaches what the entry aims it at.

[AR-08] Artisan of Copper (Artisan, Copper). A solved eigenvector for copper's lattice: cold-drawing true wire, healing verdigris pitting, tuning a bell's voice by grain. Bronze — mostly copper, as every examiner sighs — is an alloy with its own unsolved eigenvector, and the classic Eq. 4.17 cautionary example in metals guilds. Working form (Eq. 8.174): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR08, e_i in S_AR08 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Copper (AR-08): S_AR08 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR08 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-09] Artisan of Silver (Artisan, Silver). Solved for silver's lattice: mirror-finishing without polish, closing hairline cracks in plate, drawing filigree no hand-tool matches. Tarnish removal is the trade's bread; the directory notes it is the lattice being trued, not the tarnish addressed — sulfur is somebody else's eigenvector. Working form (Eq. 8.175): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR09, e_i in S_AR09 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Silver (AR-09): S_AR09 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR09 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-10] Artisan of Gold (Artisan, Gold). Solved for gold's lattice: beating leaf past any hammer's thinness, seamless joins in regalia, assay-grade surface truth. The rarest metals specialty not for difficulty but economics — patrons who can fund the eigenvector's proving already own the gold, and guard both accordingly. Working form (Eq. 8.176): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR10, e_i in S_AR10 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Gold (AR-10): S_AR10 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR10 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-11] Artisan of Tin (Artisan, Tin). Solved for tin's lattice, including its cold-weather gray-rot, which a holder can arrest or induce. The induced form once collapsed a ducal treasury's plate stock in a winter, which is why this modest eigenvector appears in three kingdoms' espionage statutes. Working form (Eq. 8.177): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR11, e_i in S_AR11 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Tin (AR-11): S_AR11 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR11 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-12] Artisan of Bronze (Artisan, Bronze). Solved for one bronze — a specific casting-alloy ratio, proven as its own eigenvector. Bell-founders' orders hold it closely. The directory stresses what §4.7 requires it to: this eigenvector covers that ratio, and a neighboring bronze is Eq. 4.17's problem, not a discount. Working form (Eq. 8.178): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR12, e_i in S_AR12 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Bronze (AR-12): S_AR12 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR12 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-13] Artisan of Oak (Artisan, Oak). Solved for oak's grain structure: seasoning decades into weeks, truing warped beams, reading — and steering — how a trunk will split. Shipwrights' yards bid for holders by name. Elm, ash, and pine are separate trees, separate eigenvectors, separate careers. Working form (Eq. 8.179): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR13, e_i in S_AR13 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Oak (AR-13): S_AR13 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR13 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-14] Artisan of Paper (Artisan, Paper). Solved for felted cellulose: mending tears fiber-to-fiber, lifting foxing, splitting a sheet into two whole leaves. Archives employ them; forgers court them; the guild examination, notoriously, includes an ethics paper — on paper the candidate must first mend. Working form (Eq. 8.180): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR14, e_i in S_AR14 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Paper (AR-14): S_AR14 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR14 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-15] Artisan of Ink (Artisan, Ink). Solved for one iron-gall formulation's bound structure: fixing fading script, lifting chosen strokes cleanly, aging a fresh line — or proving one aged. Courts in four jurisdictions seat one as an examiner of documents; courts in the other jurisdictions wish they could. Working form (Eq. 8.181): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR15, e_i in S_AR15 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Ink (AR-15): S_AR15 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR15 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-16] Artisan of Wool (Artisan, Wool). Solved for wool's fiber structure: felting without labor, un-shrinking a ruined garment, weatherproofing a cloak's weave as a lattice property rather than a grease. The homeliest eigenvector in the directory and, by guild membership rolls, the most widely held. Working form (Eq. 8.182): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR16, e_i in S_AR16 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Wool (AR-16): S_AR16 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR16 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-17] Artisan of Silk (Artisan, Silk). Solved for silk's protein lattice: reweaving tears invisibly, tuning drape and sheen, proofing thread against rot on the loom. Sericulture states treat the eigenvector's proof as a trade secret of state; at least one war of customs inspection is politely called the Silk Clarification in its winners' histories. Working form (Eq. 8.183): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR17, e_i in S_AR17 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Silk (AR-17): S_AR17 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR17 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-18] Artisan of Leather (Artisan, Leather). Solved for tanned hide — a finished material's eigenvector, distinct from AR-04's rot-pathway work on raw ones, a distinction both trades police with unusual energy. Restores suppleness, seals seams, trues stretched harness. Cavalry quartermasters rank the specialty above farriery, in writing. Working form (Eq. 8.184): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR18, e_i in S_AR18 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Leather (AR-18): S_AR18 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR18 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-19] Artisan of Ice (Artisan, Ice). Solved for water ice's crystal lattice: clear structural block from cloudy pond harvest, bridges trued across weak freezes, meltwater channels cut without a pick. Seasonal by nature — the eigenvector governs ice, not cold — and its holders famously winter in high country and summer as AR-05's envious students. Working form (Eq. 8.185): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR19, e_i in S_AR19 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Ice (AR-19): S_AR19 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR19 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-20] Artisan of Quartz (Artisan, Quartz). Solved for crystalline silica — pointedly not glass, whose amorphousness is AR-05's whole solved subject; the two specialties are each other's standing Eq. 4.17 warning. Trues lens blanks, rings time-steady chimes, cleaves crystal along chosen planes. Instrument-makers' orders underwrite the eigenvector's teaching. Working form (Eq. 8.186): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR20, e_i in S_AR20 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Quartz (AR-20): S_AR20 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR20 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-21] Artisan of Marble (Artisan, Marble). Solved for marble's calcite structure: flaw-reading before the first cut, crack-healing in standing statuary, a polish from within the stone. Temple works keep one on the fabric payroll for generations at a stretch; granite, an igneous stranger, stays strictly somebody else's stone. Working form (Eq. 8.187): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR21, e_i in S_AR21 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Marble (AR-21): S_AR21 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR21 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-22] Artisan of Granite (Artisan, Granite). Solved for one granitic family's interlocked structure: foundation truing, fortress patching, splitting along planes the quarry gods never intended to permit. The complementary specialty to AR-21 in every mason's order large enough to afford both — and the two eigenvectors, famously, share not one solved term. Working form (Eq. 8.188): Effect_i = lam_i * Fid * dAe_local * eta_AR22, e_i in S_AR22 (S per Eq. 3.1e) Working form of Eq. 4.16 for Artisan of Granite (AR-22): S_AR22 is the entry's solved eigenvector family and eta_AR22 how much of the workpiece lies within it.

[AR-23] Artisan of Chalk (Artisan, Chalk). Solved for soft calcium carbonate: hardening a chalk face against sea-collapse, drawing survey lines that sink into the stone, quarrying blocks that hold an edge they have no business holding. A coastal specialty, held mainly by two orders who between them prop up a national coastline and never tire of saying so.
